events.text: You call out twelve names at the morning drill and tell them to stay behind. The rest file off slowly, looking over their shoulders. You have had a banner sewn: {elu_name}. "This is not an honour," you tell the ones who stayed. "It is a list. When something comes up this mountain, you are who it meets first."

choices.text: Give them the east hall

effects.log: They carry their bedding across the yard in silence, and by evening someone has already carved the name over the door, badly. Nobody fixes it.

choices.text: Keep them sleeping with the others

effects.log: They stay among the rest, and the rest watch them for a year to see what changed. {elu_The} learn to be looked at.

events.text: The elders ask what a sect like yours needs with a squad that has a name. They have a point. A hall this size can barely feed itself. You tell them about the night the wall was climbed and nobody woke. Then you write {elu_name} at the top of a clean page, and you hand the brush to whoever is standing nearest.

choices.text: Let each of them write their own name under it

effects.log: Some of the hands are very bad. You keep the page anyway, in the place other sects keep their founder's sword.

choices.text: Write the names yourself

effects.log: It goes in your hand and looks official. The page is filed. They are a little quieter around you than they were.

events.text: A sect this old has a Hall for everything except the thing you want. The Discipline Hall offers you nine seniors and thirty objections. In the end you pick from the training yard yourself, walking down the line with your hands behind you, and the old rolls get a new heading: {elu_name}. The ink is the only new thing in the whole archive.

choices.text: Take them from every Hall, a few each

effects.log: No Hall can say you favoured another, and all of them say it anyway. The squad itself gets on rather better than its elders do.

choices.text: Take the best, and hear about it later

effects.log: You do hear about it later, at every council for a year. The squad is very good.

events.text: Your predecessors led this sect from a chair. You have just told the elders you mean to keep a blade in your own hand as well, and that its name is {elu_name}. Nobody objects aloud. The Keeper of the Rolls asks only how it is spelled, and whether it is to be entered before or after the kitchen accounts.

choices.text: "Before."

effects.log: It goes in before. The Keeper blots it with great care, and the whole mountain knows by supper.

choices.text: "After. Let them earn the line."

effects.log: It goes in after the turnips. {elu_The} find out, and take it as a joke, and then as a challenge.

events.text: At the long table, between the fish and the rice, you say the clan will keep a company of its own from now on, and that it will be called {elu_name}. Your aunts look at each other. Somebody asks who pays. You had hoped to get through the fish first.

choices.text: "The clan pays. Me first."

effects.log: You push your own silver down the table. It is not a lot, but it stops the question. Two cousins and a groom ask to join before the rice is cold.

choices.text: "Whoever wants to sleep safe."

effects.log: That gets a laugh from the wrong end of the table, and a purse from the right one. It will do.

events.text: The boundary stones have been moved again, a hand's width at a time, by neighbours who smile at weddings. You pick out the people you would want beside you on a dark road and tell them to come to the back of the granary after dark. That is where {elu_name} begins: with a lamp, some sacks, and very little ceremony.

choices.text: Walk the boundary with them that same night

effects.log: You put the stones back together, all of them, and leave them where the neighbours will see. Nobody at the next wedding mentions it.

choices.text: Give them a season to drill first

effects.log: They drill behind the granary until the cows stop looking up. The stones can wait until spring.

events.text: A house with this much history keeps a great many cousins and very few people who would actually die for it. You have the old household guard paraded, all of it, in the good armour. Then you walk down the line and tap a few shoulders. They will be {elu_name}, you say, and they answer to the head of the house and to no aunt.

choices.text: Have it entered in the house annals

effects.log: The annalist enters it, and adds a careful note on what became of the last head to try this. You read the note. You leave it in.

choices.text: Keep it out of the annals for now

effects.log: For a generation or so it will be a rumour with very good boots. You find you prefer it.

events.text: The tablets go back further than the province does. You stand before them with the muster book and tell your ancestors, who cannot object, that from today the house has a sword with a name: {elu_name}. Behind you a very old uncle clears his throat and says that the last one was called something similar.

choices.text: Ask him what became of it

effects.log: He tells you all of it. It takes until dawn and it is not a happy story. You make two changes to the rules before breakfast.

choices.text: "Then they will know the way."

effects.log: He laughs until somebody has to hold him up. It is all over the house by noon, and they say it in the guard room with some pride.

events.text: The Guards Division has eleven regiments, four of them ceremonial and two of them owned by the Grand Secretary's nephews. You would like a few people who are simply yours. {elu_name} appears on no budget. It draws its rice from the Imperial Stables, under a heading you wrote yourself, and the censors will find it within the year.

choices.text: Tell the censors first

effects.log: The Censor-in-Chief is so startled to be told anything that the memorial against you comes out almost polite.

choices.text: Let them find it

effects.log: They find it. You read the memorial with interest, and note who wrote which part.

events.text: Every emperor who died in the palace died among people sworn to protect the throne. It is an old joke and nobody tells it where you can hear. You sit up late with the rolls of the frontier armies, looking for those who have never once been to the capital and owe nobody here anything. They arrive in plain coats. {elu_name}, you tell them.

choices.text: Quarter them next to your own rooms

effects.log: The eunuchs of the inner palace go very quiet. For the first time in your reign you sleep past the third watch.

choices.text: Keep them outside the walls, ready

effects.log: They camp at the Western Hunting Park and appear to be doing nothing. Everyone at court can see them doing it.

events.text: The seal in your hand belongs to a child, and everyone at court keeps reminding you. A regent with a squad of their own is a regent someone will write a poem about. You raise {elu_name} anyway, and enter it in the boy's name, and you make very sure you are seen doing that part.

choices.text: Swear them to the child, before witnesses

effects.log: They kneel to a seven-year-old, who asks whether he may hold a spear. Nobody at court can say a word against it, and that was the idea.

choices.text: Swear them to the seal

effects.log: It is a fine distinction. The Grand Secretary notices it within the hour, and bows to you a little lower and a little later.

events.text: You have read the histories. Regents end in two ways, and neither is retirement. So when the old general says a hand on the seal should also have a hand on a sword, you do not pretend to be shocked. By the next new moon the palace has a new name to whisper: {elu_name}.

choices.text: Choose them from nobody's faction

effects.log: There are fewer such people than you hoped. The ones you find are excellent, and quite alone, and they know whose fault it would be if you fell.

choices.text: Take a few from every faction

effects.log: Now everyone has a friend in your squad, and so everyone is reassured, and so everyone is reading your mail.

events.text: The Cult has Squad Captains by the hundred and none of them is yours. You walk the black pillars with a list, and the ones you stop in front of go very still. They will wear the same robes. They will answer to a different name: {elu_name}. The Elders hear of it before you reach the end of the hall, which is how you know you chose well.

choices.text: Make the first of them read the oath aloud

effects.log: The voice shakes, and then it does not. The hall of pillars carries it a long way down.

choices.text: No oath. They know what you are

effects.log: There is no ceremony at all. Somehow it frightens the Elders more, and you hear of it from three of them.

events.text: In the Hundred Thousand Mountains a name has to be taken from someone. You send your chosen up against the Black Drum Hundred at the autumn trial and tell them the prize is a word on a banner. They come back bruised and short one tooth among them. From tonight they are {elu_name}, and the Drums will be remembering it.

choices.text: Feast them in front of the Elders

effects.log: The wine you pour for them is the best in the hall. Nobody touches it until you raise your cup of tea, and everybody counts who drinks to you.

choices.text: Send them straight back out

effects.log: They have been awake for two days. They go out again without being told twice, and that is noticed too.

events.text: At the Blood Altar every title is older than the language it was written in. You have brought a new one anyway. The Elders listen with their eyes closed. {elu_name}, you say again, and the oldest of them repeats it slowly, tasting it, and tells you the altar will remember whoever wears it, for as long as it finds that useful.

choices.text: Have the name cut in the altar's step

effects.log: It takes a mason four days and he does not look up once. The stone has room for it. There is a lot of room, on that step, and a lot of old names.

choices.text: Paint it, so it can be washed away

effects.log: The Elders almost smile. You have understood something about this place, they think, and you do not tell them what.

events.text: The crimson robes drink to your name before every raid, and that is the trouble: they drink to everybody's, in turn. You pick out those who stopped drinking early and stayed to see who was left standing. Those are {elu_name}. They look at you the way a butcher looks at weather, and you find that restful.

choices.text: Give them the first pick of the stores

effects.log: The other captains take note. There is a small fire in the wrong storehouse a month later, and nothing is proved.

choices.text: Give them nothing yet

effects.log: They expected nothing. They are the only people in this place who are never disappointed.

events.text: The Ashen Ghost Sect does not hold parades. You go down to the urn gallery at night and call a name softly, and then another. Those who answer come up out of the dark with ash on their sleeves. {elu_name}, you tell them. One of them asks whether the dead are to be counted in the roster. You say that depends on them.

choices.text: Count them

effects.log: The roster is longer than you can feed, and very quiet. Rivals find this hard to plan for.

choices.text: Count only the breathing

effects.log: A very old voice somewhere in the gallery sounds faintly disappointed. The ones you named look relieved.

events.text: Grief is the only thing the sect has ever had plenty of. You ask each of them who they lost and write it down beside their name, and then you close the book. {elu_name} is written on the cover in grey. "Nobody will read it," you say. "But I will know why you get up in the morning."

choices.text: Keep the book by your bed

effects.log: It sits there for years. You read it more often than you would admit, and it is why you remember all their names.

choices.text: Burn it, in front of them

effects.log: It catches slowly. They watch it the way they watch everything. Later, one of them tells you nobody has done that for them before.

events.text: The great sects have lent the Alliance men for three hundred years, and every one of them still answers to home. You ask each sect for one fighter it would rather not lose. The letters you get back are masterpieces. In the end you have a dozen people from a dozen mountains, all of them sulking, and a new name to shout at them: {elu_name}.

choices.text: Make them eat together for a month

effects.log: By the second week they are fighting. By the fourth they are fighting everyone else. It is the best morning of your leadership.

choices.text: Keep each sect's colours on them

effects.log: The sects are pleased. The squad looks like a quilt. It does not stop them from winning, and it will not stop them from arguing.

events.text: You have asked the Assembly for the right to keep a squad of your own and got eleven days of speeches. On the twelfth day you stop asking. The patrol captains who were tired of the speeches meet you on the river stairs before dawn. Nobody signs anything. It is called {elu_name} because somebody had to say something.

choices.text: Announce it at the next Assembly

effects.log: The hall goes up like a kicked hive. By the end the Wudang delegate is defending you, for reasons of his own.

choices.text: Say nothing until they have won something

effects.log: They win something quite soon. The speeches that follow are shorter.

events.text: A General may keep a household guard. Nobody ever said how good. You go through the rolls of your own banner, past the sons of important people, to the sergeants who brought their squads home. They come to your tent looking worried. "{elu_name}," you say. "Bring your own boots. The Ministry will not be paying for these."

choices.text: Pay for it out of your own pocket

effects.log: It takes most of your year. The sergeants have never in their lives seen a general pay for anything, and they tell everyone.

choices.text: Find it somewhere in the fodder accounts

effects.log: A great many horses eat very well on paper from now on. It is a matter of time before someone counts them.

events.text: Every battle you have won turned on a few people who did not run at the moment when running made sense. You have written down those moments, and the people. Now you have them all in one tent, and most of them have never met. They will march at your stirrup under a name of their own: {elu_name}.

choices.text: Tell each of them what you saw them do

effects.log: It takes a while. Some of them had no idea anyone saw. The tent is very quiet by the end.

choices.text: Tell them only where to stand

effects.log: They find their places. It is an army. Nobody expected a speech, and by tomorrow they will have made up their own.

events.text: The first thing {elu_the} ask is what they are permitted. In this house it is a fair question. The abbot's word for it is "the shield hand", and it took four hundred years of argument to arrive at. {elu_oath} You look along the row of shaved or bowed heads. Each of them has already decided what to do on the day it is not enough.

choices.text: Add one line: "and you will tell me after"

effects.log: They do, for years, at odd hours. It turns out that you are the one who loses sleep.

choices.text: Leave the old words as they stand

effects.log: They say it three times, and it holds as well as it ever held anyone.

events.text: You had meant to say something about duty. The oldest of {elu_the} is watching a leaf go round in the fountain and says the river has never once sworn to anybody. {elu_oath} It is not at all what you wrote down, and it is what they will repeat to each other at the gate.

choices.text: Throw your paper in the fountain

effects.log: It goes round with the leaf. They seem to find this a much better oath than the one you had, and you suppose you have just sworn it.

choices.text: Read it out anyway

effects.log: They listen kindly. You will find it quoted back at you, usually at an awkward moment.

events.text: The rites for a thing like this do not exist, so somebody has found some. {elu_the} kneel in the proper order, and the order takes an hour to establish. {elu_oath} You hold the cup, and your arms ache, and you begin to see what ceremony is really for: nobody here will ever say they did not know what they were promising.

choices.text: Drink, and hand the cup down the row

effects.log: It reaches the last of them nearly empty. They drink what is there. Someone has been keeping count of who drank how much, and of course they have.

choices.text: Have the words carved for the gate

effects.log: It is expensive. It is also the first thing anybody visiting will read.

events.text: They want it done with a blade across the palm, the way it is in the stories, and you tell them that a hand that is cut does not hold a sword as well. So it is only words, out in the yard, with the wind taking half of them. {elu_oath} Someone at the back repeats it twice, in case the first one did not count.

choices.text: Answer with an oath of your own to them

effects.log: You had not planned on that. Neither had they. It is much harder to send people into the dark after you have said it to their faces.

choices.text: Nod, and dismiss them

effects.log: They go off to supper talking loudly. You are the only one in the yard who knows how it tends to end.

events.text: The oath is short. It is whatever the strongest of them says it is, and so they settle that first, in the mud, with you watching. It takes most of an afternoon. {elu_oath} The winner spits out something small, and grins, and says that will do. The rest of them seem to agree.

choices.text: Then put the winner on their back yourself

effects.log: It takes about a breath. Nobody needs the oath explained to them after that.

choices.text: Pay for everyone's bandages

effects.log: They are not sure what to make of that. A few of them keep the bandage cloth, which you find out years later.

events.text: Every house has a way of making sure. In yours, it comes in a small lidded cup, and it is only fair to say so. The apothecary explains: a dose that does nothing, for as long as they come home every year for the other half. {elu_oath} Nobody flinches. They grew up here. Some of them have opinions about the recipe.

choices.text: Drink the first cup yourself

effects.log: It tastes of almonds and bad decisions. There is nothing they can say to you after that, and no one can ever say you asked what you would not do.

choices.text: Empty the cups on the ground

effects.log: The grass there will not grow back for years. It is the first time anybody in this house has been trusted, and it makes them deeply uneasy.

events.text: The Cult has an oath for everything, and every one of them ends with the same words. {elu_oath} {elu_The} say it with their eyes on you. You know what they are doing: looking for the place they would put the knife, if it came to that. It is what you would do. That is why you chose them.

choices.text: Show them the place

effects.log: You open your collar and tap it. There is a long silence, then a laugh, from somewhere, and it does not sound afraid.

choices.text: Let them keep looking

effects.log: Good. You would think less of them if they stopped. It keeps everybody polite.

events.text: They bring the bowl, and the bowl is older than the Altar. It is only a red wine now, or so the Elders say, with a straight face, as the Elders always do. {elu_oath} You watch it go down the row, and you watch the ones who look into it first, and you make a note.

choices.text: Pour yours back

effects.log: It is not done. The Elders open their eyes. You have told them something, and they are deciding what.

choices.text: Raise the bowl as they do, and pass it on

effects.log: It smells of only wine. It nearly always is. {elu_The} stand a little closer on the way out.

events.text: The first real test of {elu_the} is nothing you planned. A caravan of your own people has been stopped at a ford by somebody with a grudge and a dozen hired spears. {elu_m} looks at you and asks whether this is the sort of thing the unit is for. It is a good question. You are about to answer it for good.

choices.text: "This is exactly what it is for"

effects.log: They are gone for three days. They come back with the caravan, the spears and a very embarrassed person who would like to apologise.

choices.text: "Go, but bring everyone back"

effects.log: They take longer, and they bring everyone back. They are a little disappointed. You find that you are not.

events.text: A boy turns up with a letter for {elu_the}, and it takes a moment to understand that this means you. Somebody in the next county has heard of your people and would like to hire them. The offer is rude and rather large. {elu_m} has read it twice already and is pretending not to have.

choices.text: Refuse it, and send them a copy of the oath

effects.log: The boy carries it back looking pleased. It gets read out in a tavern, and a good deal of it is repeated around the county, slightly improved.

choices.text: Take the silver, this once

effects.log: It is a dull job and it pays for the winter. {elu_The} learn what they are worth, and that you know the figure too.

events.text: Two of {elu_the} have fought in the yard over who stands on the left. It is a stupid thing to fight about. It is the only thing they have to fight about so far, and half the sect has come to watch. {elu_m} has a split lip and refuses to say who started it.

choices.text: Put them both on the left, side by side, for a month

effects.log: They hate it. Then the left side of the line turns out to be the strongest thing you own.

choices.text: Let them finish it

effects.log: They finish it. It takes a long time. They share a bowl of something afterwards and do not speak of it again.

events.text: Somebody has painted the name of {elu_the} on the side of the granary, and put a very rude drawing beneath it. There is a small crowd. It is, you have to admit, a good likeness. {elu_m} comes to ask whether they are to find out who did it, and has obviously brought a list.

choices.text: Have them leave it there

effects.log: It stays for years. Visitors ask about it. {elu_The} end up rather proud of it, and they touch it for luck before they ride out.

choices.text: Have it scrubbed, quietly, and find the artist

effects.log: The artist turns out to be eleven. You give the child some better paint. The next one is much better, and just as rude.

events.text: Salt carts, sixty of them, coming through the pass at the worst possible time of year, and every bandit between here and the river knows it. {elu_m} has been up all night over the map. {elu_The} can take the high road and be seen, or go ahead of the carts by a day and make sure nobody is waiting.

choices.text: The high road, banners out

effects.log: You tell {elu_m} to let them see the name. Anyone who wants to try it should know what they are trying.

choices.text: A day ahead, no banners

effects.log: You tell {elu_m} to go quietly and count everything. It will be slow, and dull, and that is the plan.

events.text: A magistrate you have done business with writes that a county has stopped sending anything down the river road. No bandits have been named, and nobody who goes to look comes back to say. {elu_m} asks how many of {elu_the} you would like to send.

choices.text: All of them, at once

effects.log: Better to be too many. {elu_m} nods and goes to wake them, and you can hear it through the wall.

choices.text: Three, in plain coats, to look

effects.log: Three go off with mules. If this goes well, nobody will ever know it needed doing.

events.text: A bride is being taken across two provinces with a dowry anyone can see from a mile off, and the families are paying well to have it arrive. The bride has already sent a note to {elu_m}, asking to be taught how to hold a knife on the way.

choices.text: Ride close and look dangerous

effects.log: They ride close. It is mostly a matter of looking at people until they find something else to do.

choices.text: Teach her, and keep the road ahead clear

effects.log: It is against several customs. {elu_m} is teaching a very quick student by the second day, and scouting the fords by the third.

events.text: The plague cart road has to stay open, and the villages along it have started blocking it with their own carts. They are frightened, and nobody wants to be the one to make them move. {elu_m} has asked you what {elu_the} are to do about frightened people who are armed with hoes.

choices.text: Open the road, fast

effects.log: Fast is kinder, you tell {elu_m}, and you are nearly sure. They go out at first light.

choices.text: Talk first, village by village

effects.log: It will cost weeks, and the carts will wait. {elu_m} takes the one who is good with old people.

events.text: A rival's storehouse sits on a hill a day from here, and it has a fat lock and a thin guard. You did not get the plan from anyone respectable. {elu_m} has been to look and came back thoughtful. It can be done at night with nobody hurt, nearly. Or it can be done at noon, so that everyone knows who did it.

choices.text: At noon, with the banner

effects.log: Let them explain that to their neighbours. {elu_m} starts to grin, and tries to stop.

choices.text: At night, and leave no name

effects.log: Nobody will ever be able to say. {elu_m} looks a little sorry about that, and goes to find soft shoes.

events.text: There is a toll gate on the river that used to be somebody's and is now, through a marriage nobody liked, somebody else's. Everyone hates the toll. If {elu_the} took it down, you would be a hero in three towns and an enemy in one very large house. {elu_m} is looking at you with a certain expression.

choices.text: Burn the gate down

effects.log: They bring a lot of oil and a certain amount of joy. {elu_m} sends you the gatekeeper's hat.

choices.text: Quietly buy the debt, and take it by law

effects.log: It takes a dozen visits and a very frightened clerk. {elu_The} spend a season standing behind people at meetings.

events.text: The Greenwood has a camp in the hills above your southern farms, and it has been taking one cow in ten for four years. They have started to call it rent. {elu_m} asks, carefully, whether this mission is to end the camp, or only the rent.

choices.text: End the camp

effects.log: {elu_m} nods. There is nothing else to discuss. They leave before the rain does.

choices.text: Take their horses, and let them think about it

effects.log: A camp with no horses has a long walk to anywhere. {elu_m} seems to find this funnier than you do.

events.text: There is an old quarrel with a house across the valley, and they have just buried their strongest elder. Everybody knows it. It is exactly the moment when decent people send a condolence gift. {elu_m} has already saddled up, and is waiting to hear whether the gift is to be delivered with or without the rest of it.

choices.text: Without the gift

effects.log: It is an ugly thing and it will work. {elu_The} ride out without looking at each other much.

choices.text: With the gift, and very good manners

effects.log: {elu_m} delivers it in full armour, and stays for tea, and counts every spear in the house while drinking it.

events.text: You have started to feel watched in your own hall. {elu_m} has a way of being the last person to leave a room and has noticed some things: a new cook, a letter that went out with no reason to, a junior with money. The quiet way to do this takes a year. There is also a loud way.

choices.text: Turn the hall upside down

effects.log: Everyone will know, and whoever it is will run. Someone is sure to run. {elu_m} goes off to find a very large stick.

choices.text: Leave them in place, and watch

effects.log: They keep the cook. It is a hard thing to go on eating. {elu_m} stops looking at anyone directly.

events.text: A man in a teahouse in the provincial capital claims to know what your enemies are planning, and he wants more than he is worth. {elu_m} suggests that a person who is willing to sell to you has probably sold to others. You could buy what he has. You could also have him followed home.

choices.text: Grab him tonight, and ask

effects.log: It may not be subtle. {elu_m} takes two of the large ones and nobody takes any tea.

choices.text: Follow him for a season

effects.log: He is a dull man with a surprising number of friends. {elu_m} takes up residence over a noodle shop.

events.text: Letters are passing between two of your oldest allies, and neither has mentioned it. It is probably nothing. {elu_m} has already found out that the courier stops at the same inn every month, and that the innkeeper has a son who needs a job.

choices.text: Open the letters on the road

effects.log: It means somebody will know soon. {elu_m} shrugs and takes the sharpest knife to the sealing wax.

choices.text: Hire the son, and wait

effects.log: A year goes by. The son turns out to be good at this. You are not sure whether that should worry you.

events.text: There is a rumour that someone from your own unit has been seen in the wrong city, in the wrong company, at the wrong hour. {elu_m} brought it to you, which is either loyalty or very good cover. You could set the rest of them to find out. You would have to live with what they then think of each other.

choices.text: Put it to them openly, at supper

effects.log: You lay it on the table with the rice. Nobody eats. {elu_m} watches the door.

choices.text: Have {elu_m} look into it alone

effects.log: One pair of eyes, nobody told. It takes a year off {elu_m}, and you see that it does.

events.text: The war with {elu_foe} has come to where it was always going to come. Your side has the numbers on paper. {elu_m} brings the plan for {elu_the}: a night climb up the back of the enemy's position, thirty people and a great deal of rope. Or they can stay in the line, where they are the only thing the line is sure of.

choices.text: Send them up the rope

effects.log: If it works it ends the season. {elu_m} takes the rope and goes to check every knot.

choices.text: Keep them in the line

effects.log: The line holds. It does not win anything, and {elu_the} say so.

choices.text: Hold them back, for later

effects.log: There is going to be a later. You tell them so, and they do not like it.

events.text: A messenger from {elu_foe} comes to your gate under a white flag and asks, with great politeness, whether {elu_the} are to be in the coming fight. They have a rather good idea who is on your rolls, and it says something that they sent to ask. {elu_m} is standing right behind you when the question comes.

choices.text: "Tell them to look for the name"

effects.log: The messenger bows and goes. {elu_m} has the banner mended that night.

choices.text: "Tell them nothing, and feed the messenger"

effects.log: The messenger eats well, and counts your horses, which is why you put them there. Your people go where they are needed.

events.text: Everyone on your side knows about {elu_the} now, and that is becoming the trouble. Lesser captains are holding back and waiting for your people to do the hard part. {elu_m} comes to you quite tired, and asks if there is any part of this war that {elu_the} are not expected to fight.

choices.text: Put them at the very front again

effects.log: They go. {elu_m} does not ask again. The others can see, at any rate, what it looks like.

choices.text: Spread them out among the weak companies

effects.log: It makes every company a little better, and nobody a legend. {elu_m} stops looking so tired.

choices.text: Rest them this season

effects.log: They sleep for three days. Some of the others say things about it. They are not said twice.

events.text: It is a bad season. {elu_foe} has something new, some trick of the ground you did not expect, and your people have been falling back for a month. {elu_m} comes in with mud to the waist and says that what {elu_the} can do is one of two things: buy you a week, or be alive to fight next year.

choices.text: Buy the week

effects.log: You watch {elu_m} take that in. Then they go out, and you get your week.

choices.text: Pull them out

effects.log: They fall back with the rest, and they hate you for it, and they are alive.

events.text: Two armies have been looking at each other across a river for three weeks. It is all very dull and everyone is ill. {elu_m} suggests that a champion of {elu_foe} has been crossing to the same fishing rock every morning, and that it would not be difficult. It would not be at all honourable, either.

choices.text: Do it

effects.log: The enemy lines wake up without a champion. Nobody on your side says anything. Everyone on your side knows who.

choices.text: Go and fish beside them, and talk

effects.log: You sit there all morning. It is not what anybody expected, and you learn a good deal about the state of their rations.

events.text: The war has gone on long enough that {elu_the} have recruits who have never known anything else. {elu_m} has them drilling on the same ground where the last lot died, because it is flat. They ask whether you would like to say something to them before they go up against {elu_foe}.

choices.text: Tell them the truth of it

effects.log: It is short and not very encouraging. They seem steadier afterwards, and you do not fully understand why.

choices.text: Tell them who they are

effects.log: You say the name, and what it has done. You watch their chins come up. You remember the last time you did this, and you go on anyway.

events.text: A long way from anywhere you have heard of, {elu_m} has written. They have the banner of {elu_the} in a country where nobody can pronounce it, and the locals have started to call them something else, with a certain respect. The letter asks for boots, in some detail. It does not ask when they are coming home.

choices.text: Send the boots, and a good deal more

effects.log: It takes half a year to get there. The next letter is mostly about how well the boots fit.

choices.text: Send a note: hold what you have

effects.log: They hold it. The next letter is rather shorter.

events.text: The generals have begun asking for {elu_the} by name, each for their own front, and each with excellent reasons. It is a nice problem to have. {elu_m} has heard about it, and sends word that {elu_the} would be glad to be split up, and will find it very hard to forgive you.

choices.text: Keep them together

effects.log: The generals sulk. {elu_The} win something large in the spring, all in one place.

choices.text: Split them among the fronts

effects.log: Every front gets a little harder, and nobody remembers quite who did what. {elu_m} stops writing for a while.

events.text: You took the region; nobody has told the region. {elu_The} have been left to hold a pass while the army goes on, and the people of the pass have been bringing them food, for reasons {elu_m} cannot quite work out. There is a wedding invitation. Two of your people seem to want to stay.

choices.text: Let them stay and marry

effects.log: Now you have two farmers in the pass who know how to fight, and a village that stops being a problem.

choices.text: Order them back to the march

effects.log: They come. The village watches them go, and the pass is a little less friendly the next time anybody uses it.

events.text: A captured commander says that where they come from, they tell stories about {elu_the} to make children behave. {elu_m} sends this along as a joke. You read it several times. There was a time when you would have had to explain what the name even meant.

choices.text: Have it added to the unit's rolls

effects.log: It goes in under Honours, in a clerk's very straight hand: "Used to frighten children, in four languages."

choices.text: Tell them not to enjoy it

effects.log: They take this in the spirit it was intended, which is to say they enjoy it enormously, somewhat further away.

events.text: {elu_m} has started coming down to the yard an hour before anyone else. You assumed it was devotion. Then you see how long it takes to get the left knee to bend in the morning, and how carefully it is done where nobody can see. They catch you looking. "I know how old I am," they say. "So does the knee. Nobody else needs to."

choices.text: Say nothing, and move the drill back an hour

effects.log: Nobody remarks on it. {elu_m} looks at you for some time when the new hours go up, and is exactly on time.

choices.text: Offer {em_him} an easier post

effects.log: You say it kindly. {elu_m} hears you out, and thanks you, and is an hour early the next morning as well.

events.text: It happens on a stair, on a mission that should have been simple. The knee goes. The younger ones get {elu_m} out, and nobody says anything about it, very loudly. There is a post open teaching recruits. It is a good post. {elu_m} has brought you the letter resigning from {elu_the}, and is holding it out and watching your face.

choices.text: Tear it up

effects.log: "Then I will need a stick," {elu_m} says. "Get one," you say. It is a very good stick, in the end, and it hits harder than you would think.

choices.text: Take it, and hold the post open a year

effects.log: "A year," {elu_m} says. Neither of you believes it. {em_He} stays on to pack very slowly.

events.text: Something has gone wrong at the bridge, and the rest of {elu_the} are on the far bank. {elu_m} is on the near one, with the stick, and with the people who are coming. {em_He} looks back across at you. It is too far to shout, and there is no need. The bridge is narrow, and somebody could hold it for quite a while, at least until the knee goes.

choices.text: Let {em_him} have the bridge

effects.log: You will not forget it. When it is over they bring you the stick, and the bridge has a name now, and it is not one the map-makers chose.

choices.text: Go back for {em_him}

effects.log: It is a stupid risk, and it costs you some skin. {elu_m} calls you several things on the way back, and then takes the recruits' post without another word. The recruits come out of it terrifying.

events.text: You find out by accident that half of what you pay {elu_m} goes to a moneylender in the river town, and has done for eleven years. Some parent's debt, grown to the size of a house. {elu_m} goes very stiff when you bring it up. "It does not affect my work." It does not, so far.

choices.text: Offer to clear it

effects.log: "No." Then, later, in the yard: "I will think about it." {em_He} does not mention it again.

choices.text: Let {em_him} keep {em_his} pride

effects.log: You leave it. {em_He} works a little harder for a while, as if someone had given {em_him} something.

events.text: The moneylender has sold the note. The new holder is very polite, and has asked to see {elu_m}, and has a good idea who {elu_m} works for. {em_He} tells you all this, standing at attention, in a voice with nothing in it. Somebody has noticed there is a door into {elu_the}, and that it has a price.

choices.text: Buy the note yourself, tonight

effects.log: It costs more than it should. They were expecting you, and you pay it. You put the note in a drawer and tell {elu_m} it is there.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to meet them, and report back

effects.log: It is a dangerous thing to ask of a tired person. {elu_m} goes down to the river with {em_his} face shut.

events.text: Somebody has been asking {elu_m} small questions: where {elu_the} will be, and when, and how many. One small answer would buy off the whole of it, and there is a note with a very large number on it. {em_He} has come to your room after dark and has put a purse down on your table. "This is what they gave me for last month," {em_he} says. "I gave them nothing true. I do not know how long I can go on."

choices.text: Clear the debt, whatever it costs

effects.log: You go down to the river yourself with a good many people. It costs a lot, one way and another. {elu_m} is your own after that, and you never need to ask again.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to keep lying to them

effects.log: It works for two years. Then one evening {elu_m} is gone, and the purse is on the table, and it is a good deal heavier. You never find out which answer was true.

choices.text: Let {em_him} go, with your thanks

effects.log: {elu_m} looks at you for a while, and then bows, and goes. It is the cleanest thing either of you could think of. You still think about it.

events.text: At a market, a stranger sees {elu_m} and goes white, and says a name that is not the one on your rolls. {elu_m} goes on buying onions. Later {em_he} tells you, quite calmly, that {em_he} served with {elu_rv} once, and that {em_he} did not exactly hand in {em_his} notice.

choices.text: "Who else knows?"

effects.log: "Now? That one," {elu_m} says. "So by the end of the month, everyone." You appreciate being told. {em_He} goes back to the onions.

choices.text: "You should have told me."

effects.log: "Yes," {elu_m} says, and nothing else. It is a long time before {em_he} tells you anything again.

events.text: A letter has come for you from {elu_rvc} of {elu_rv}. It is courteous, and short. It says that one of {elu_the} once left their service in the middle of a fight, leaving several people to die, and it asks for {elu_m} back, to be dealt with. {elu_m} has read it over your shoulder without asking. "It was not several," {em_he} says. "It was two. I knew them both."

choices.text: Reply: they are mine now

effects.log: You write it out in your own hand. {elu_m} takes it to the courier personally, and {em_he} does not say thank you, and {em_he} never leaves your left side again.

choices.text: Ask what really happened

effects.log: It takes until morning. It does not make {em_him} look any better, or any worse. You still have not answered the letter.

events.text: They have come, and they did it properly: {elu_rvc} and a dozen of {elu_rv} are at your gate at noon, with no weapons drawn. {elu_m} has already put on {em_his} old colours from the bottom of a chest. "I can end this," {em_he} says. "It is a duel, under their rules. Or you can make it a war, and I would be ashamed of that for the rest of my life, however long it is."

choices.text: Let {em_him} fight it

effects.log: It takes less time than you had thought. {elu_rvc} kneels by {elu_m} afterwards, and says something only the two of them can hear, and has the old colours folded and given to you.

choices.text: Walk out and stand beside {em_him}

effects.log: You stand there through the whole of it. {elu_rvc} looks at you for a long moment and has the charge struck from their rolls, "for now." {elu_m} rises in {elu_the} until nobody remembers the other name.

events.text: Nobody ever remarks on {elu_m}. {em_He} is in the middle of the line, does what is asked, and eats what there is. Then you see {em_him} alone behind the woodshed, doing one of your own forms at a speed that nobody taught {em_him}, and {em_he} is doing it wrong in a way that is better. {em_He} stops the moment {em_he} knows you are there.

choices.text: Show {em_him} the next form

effects.log: Neither of you says anything. {em_He} watches once, nods, and goes back to the woodshed.

choices.text: Ask where {em_he} learned it

effects.log: "Nowhere," {elu_m} says, truthfully, and is very careful after that not to be seen. You find you have made a mistake.

events.text: The whole unit has now noticed. It has become a game to try {elu_m} at the morning sparring, and nobody has won in a season. {em_He} is very apologetic. It is starting to wear on them: the old hands who gave ten years to get where {elu_m} got in two. Someone has hidden {em_his} boots, and someone else has made sure you heard about it.

choices.text: Put {em_him} in charge of the drill

effects.log: It is the worst possible idea, and it might work. {elu_m} looks horrified. By winter, the old hands are getting better, and pretending that was their own idea.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let them work it out

effects.log: They do, more or less, in a way that involves a lot of bruises and one broken bench. {elu_m} stops apologising, which helps.

events.text: {elu_m} comes to see you at the turn of the year, with a realm behind {em_his} eyes that you did not give {em_him}, and {em_he} has never been so polite. There is nothing more you can teach {em_him}. You both know it. A great house has written. So has somebody else, who offered more. {em_He} would like to know what you would do.

choices.text: Give {em_him} the captaincy of a wing

effects.log: {elu_m} thinks about it for a very long time, and takes it. Your unit has a new name to be afraid of, and it answers to you. For the time being, it does.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to go and see the world

effects.log: {em_He} bows lower than you have ever seen, and is gone by morning. You hear the name again, years on, from very far away, and {em_he} tells them who taught {em_him}.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} no: you need {em_him} here

effects.log: {em_He} stays. {em_He} goes on being very polite. One morning, years later, the best blade you ever had is simply not in the yard, nor is your war chest.

events.text: You pick up a letter {elu_m} left on the bench. It is to a younger sibling back in some county, and it describes in loving detail the work of an assistant clerk in a grain office, with complaints about the ink. {elu_m} takes it from you without hurrying. "It is easier on my mother," {em_he} says.

choices.text: Offer to have the grain office send a real stamp

effects.log: It is a very small forgery. {elu_m} stares at you, then laughs, for the first time in your hearing.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} they deserve the truth

effects.log: {em_He} nods politely. The next letter is about the ink as well.

events.text: The younger sibling has saved up and made the trip, and has walked in at your gate asking for the grain office. {elu_m} is out on a job and will be back by nightfall, with whatever is left of a bad week on {em_his} clothes. The child is sitting on your step, with a parcel of dried persimmons, looking at the banner of {elu_the}.

choices.text: Have the guards play along

effects.log: Eleven extremely dangerous people spend a whole evening discussing grain. It is the most frightened you have ever seen them.

choices.text: Tell the child the truth, gently

effects.log: The parcel stays in those hands for a long time. When {elu_m} comes in, the two of them go out to the wall, and they do not come back for hours.

events.text: The sibling has stayed, and has grown, and is now asking to join {elu_the}. {elu_m} has come to you and stood at attention. "I have done eleven years of this," {em_he} says, "so that one person in my family would never have to know how it is done. Please refuse." And then, behind {em_him}, in the doorway: "Please don't."

choices.text: Refuse, and find the child real work in a real grain office

effects.log: There is a great deal of shouting. In twenty years there is a Registrar of Grain in that county who writes to you every spring, with complaints about the ink. {elu_m} never says thanks, and never needs to. {em_He} stays with you for good.

choices.text: Take the child in

effects.log: {elu_m} says nothing at all. {em_He} trains that child harder than anyone, for three years, and then asks to be sent somewhere else. You can see why. You let {em_him} go.

choices.text: Let them settle it, on the road home

effects.log: They go off together to see their mother. Only one of them comes back, and it is {elu_m}, with some dried persimmons. Nobody asks anything else. {em_He} rises steadily, and never writes again.

events.text: You notice that when you give an order in the yard, some of {elu_the} look at {elu_m} before they move. It is very quick. It is probably nothing. {em_He} has a gift for remembering birthdays and for making sure people get paid, and {em_he} has mentioned once or twice, in a helpful way, how you might have done something better.

choices.text: Give {em_him} real authority, in the open

effects.log: Now it is your idea, at least. {elu_m} takes it with a small bow, and you see {em_him} thinking about it.

choices.text: Quietly move two of them away from {em_him}

effects.log: It works for about a month. {elu_m} sends the two of them a birthday gift.

events.text: Someone who wishes you well has sent you a copy of a toast. It was drunk at an inn on the road, by several of your people, to "{elu_m}, who ought to be leading the thing." It is possibly just a toast. {elu_m} comes to you of {em_his} own accord, the next morning, and says that you have probably heard about the toast, and that {em_he} told them not to.

choices.text: Believe {em_him}, and say so

effects.log: "Thank you," {elu_m} says, and looks at you closely, to see whether you do.

choices.text: Ask who else was there

effects.log: {em_He} tells you all the names without hesitating. It occurs to you later that those are the names {em_he} would be happy to lose.

events.text: Half of {elu_the} are standing in the yard before dawn, and they are not on your orders. {elu_m} is in front of them with {em_his} hands empty. "Nobody here means you any harm," {em_he} says. "They would just like to be led by someone who is here." It is said respectfully. It is the most dangerous thing anyone has said to you in years.

choices.text: Give {em_him} the captaincy, then and there

effects.log: You walk up and put the unit's token into {em_his} hand. There is a very long silence. You have either lost them or won them for good, and {elu_m} will take years to work out which.

choices.text: Call {em_him} out, one to one, in front of them

effects.log: It takes about four breaths. {em_He} gets up, bows, and is gone by nightfall, and so are three others. You hear of a new company on the river road.

choices.text: Dismiss {em_him}, with a pension

effects.log: The yard stays very still. {elu_m} looks round at them. Nobody moves. {em_He} takes the pension. You have won, and they will never quite forgive you for it, nor {em_him} either.

events.text: You find the place at the table empty and the unit's accounts rather lighter. {elu_m} has gone over to someone with better prospects, and {em_he} has taken what {em_he} knows. There is a note. It says, in a clear hand, exactly what you did wrong, with dates. Your people are standing around the table not looking at you.

choices.text: Send {elu_the} after {em_him}

effects.log: They bring back the accounts, and a torn sleeve. {elu_m} got away, and now everyone knows you will try.

choices.text: Read the note aloud, then burn it

effects.log: Your voice stays level, which takes some effort. The dates are correct. A few of them look at you differently now, and it is not all worse.

choices.text: Change every plan, and say nothing

effects.log: It costs a season of work. You never speak the name again, and everyone notices that you do not.

events.text: It comes by way of an old friend, who has it from a clerk: {elu_m} has been writing to the other side for some time. The clerk has seen the letters. You go through a whole day with that person standing at your left hand, as {em_he} has for years, handing you things.

choices.text: Have it out in the yard, today

effects.log: It does not take long, once it starts. {em_He} does not deny it, and {em_he} goes over the wall with blood on {em_his} sleeve and all your plans in {em_his} head.

choices.text: Offer {em_him} a way to come back

effects.log: "Why?" {elu_m} says, and it is a real question. You answer it. Whether {em_he} believes you, you will know in a year or two.

choices.text: Let {em_him} go, and let them know why

effects.log: You send {em_him} off at the gate, in front of everyone, with {em_his} wages. It is much worse than a fight, and {em_he} knows it.

events.text: You come back to find that {elu_m} has taken the banner of {elu_the} down from the hall and has walked off with it. It was the original, the bad one. The rest of them are furious, and also a little impressed. A letter arrives within the month, under another house's seal, asking what you would take for its return.

choices.text: Refuse, and have another one sewn

effects.log: The new one is much better made. Nobody likes it. You will see the old one again one day, in someone's hall, and they will make sure of it.

choices.text: Pay for it

effects.log: It comes back washed, in a very nice box. {elu_m} has signed the receipt, for which there was no need at all.

events.text: Word has come from {elu_rv}: they have a new captain of a wing, and it is {elu_m}. {em_He} has told them your drills and your signals and the name of the one who talks in their sleep. Someone on your side has already asked whether they should change the signals, or kill someone.

choices.text: Change the signals. Only the signals

effects.log: It takes months. In a way the new ones are better. Somewhere, {elu_m} would be the first to say so.

choices.text: Put a price on {em_him}

effects.log: It is quite a large price. It feels very good for about an hour.

events.text: A company has appeared in your way on the river road, under a banner you have seen before. {elu_m} has aged. So have you. {em_He} rides out to the middle of the ford, alone, with {em_his} hands in plain sight, and says that {em_he} has been meaning to ask how the knee is, and whether you ever worked out the thing with the dates.

choices.text: Ride out, and finish it

effects.log: It goes on longer than you remembered it could. You ride back and {em_he} does not, and {elu_the} stand aside as you pass, and you do not feel at all as you had thought you would.

choices.text: Ride out, and offer {em_him} the old place

effects.log: "You always were an idiot," {elu_m} says, and rides over with {em_his} whole company. There is a great deal of trouble about it in the unit. You do not regret it, most days.

events.text: You get a parcel. There is no letter, just a worn-out token of {elu_the}, the old kind, and a name and an hour written on a slip of paper: someone is coming for you, and this is when. It proves accurate. You only ever had one enemy who wrote that neatly. A long way off, {elu_m} is apparently still keeping accounts.

choices.text: Send back the token, with a note: "Paid"

effects.log: Nothing comes back. Nothing needs to. {elu_The} keep the old rolls open at that page for a long time.

choices.text: Go and find {em_him}, to ask why

effects.log: You find a small house and a small grave. A neighbour says there was a list of things to do, and that yours was the last. You stand there a while.

events.text: There is a plot, and you know it, and now someone has gone to {elu_m} with a purse. {elu_m} has come directly to you with the purse, and has put it on the table. You weigh it in your hand. It is a remarkably large sum, for such a small thing as your life. {em_He} is watching you do it.

choices.text: Push it back to {em_him}: "Keep it. You earned that."

effects.log: {elu_m} looks at the purse, and then at you. {em_He} takes it, and pays for the entire unit's dinner with it, and never speaks of it again.

choices.text: Have {em_him} take the purse, and tell them yes

effects.log: Now you have somebody inside. {elu_m} goes off to be a traitor for a season, with a look on {em_his} face that you cannot quite read.

events.text: You have reason to think that somebody in {elu_the} has been bought. You do not know who. {elu_m} says, with a straight face, that it might be {em_him}, and that you should probably check. You could feed each of them a different false plan and see which one comes back. It would work. They would also find out, sooner or later.

choices.text: Feed them the false plans

effects.log: It works. It takes months, and you find out what you find out, and when they learn of it, no one is very surprised, and nobody quite forgets.

choices.text: Trust them. All of them

effects.log: You say so at supper, with the whole table listening. It may be the stupidest thing you have done. It is very quiet, and somebody passes you the rice.

events.text: {elu_m} has been missing from the drill. You find {em_him} in a wine shop, in the middle of the day, in the company of someone who knows your enemies very well indeed. They both look up. {elu_m} gets to {em_his} feet, not quite steady. "I can explain this," {em_he} says, "but not in here."

choices.text: Sit down at their table

effects.log: You order a jug. The other one goes a very odd colour. {elu_m} sits down again slowly, and you can see {em_him} deciding something.

choices.text: Walk out, and set a watch on {em_him}

effects.log: It may be nothing. You have to know. {elu_m} sees the watcher by the second day, and waves, without much humour.

events.text: The names of the plotters have come to you, and one of them keeps on turning up in {elu_the}: an old friend of {elu_m}, godparent to a child, a person who has eaten at your own table. {elu_m} has heard. {em_He} asks to be the one sent. "If it is someone else, I will always wonder what they said," {em_he} says.

choices.text: Send {em_him}

effects.log: You do not ask what was said. {elu_m} is gone for a month and comes back thinner, and is never again wrong about anything to do with you.

choices.text: Send someone else

effects.log: It is the safer thing. It is done, and done well. {elu_m} goes on with {em_his} work and does not bring it up.

events.text: You had been told that they would try to turn your people. What you had not expected was a formal offer, in a good hand, addressed to {elu_the} as a body: double wages, a full pardon for everything, and a place in what comes after you. {elu_m} has read it aloud at supper to the whole unit. It has got rather a large laugh, but not from everybody.

choices.text: Ask who did not laugh

effects.log: You have a list by morning, from {elu_m}. It is a short list. You look at it for a long time before you decide what it is for.

choices.text: Double their wages yourself

effects.log: It is ruinous. Nobody laughs at that, and everybody has a very good year.

events.text: {elu_m} is dead. They bring you what there is: a token, a good knife, a bad letter somebody will now have to finish. The rest of {elu_the} have gone quiet in the way they do. There is a custom about this by now, you find. Someone is waiting for you to say which one of them moves up to the empty place.

choices.text: Say the name out loud, in the yard

effects.log: You say it once, and they say it back. It is the only sound on the mountain. You think it carries a long way.

choices.text: Finish the letter yourself

effects.log: It takes you all night. It is to a sibling. You do not know what {em_he} meant to say at the end, so you say what you would have.

events.text: There is no body. There is a place where {elu_m} was last seen, and a person who says they saw it, and the river. {elu_The} go on setting {em_his} bowl for two months, and you do not tell them to stop. Then one night someone turns it over, gently, and nobody asks who.

choices.text: Have {em_his} name added to the banner

effects.log: A small stitched line. They fight over who gets to do the stitching, and it comes out crooked.

choices.text: Pay what is owed to {em_his} family

effects.log: It is not what anyone would call enough. You deliver it yourself. Nobody there knew what {em_he} did for a living, and you do not tell them all of it.

events.text: It was old age, in the end, which nobody in {elu_the} had seriously planned for. {elu_m} went in {em_his} sleep, with {em_his} boots by the bed, in a neat row. They have been arguing all morning over whether it counts. A very young one asks you whether there is a proper way to do this, when no one has anybody to blame.

choices.text: "Yes. Tell stories, and lie."

effects.log: It takes three days. By the end {elu_m} had fought a river. {em_He} would have corrected every word of it.

choices.text: "No. Sit with it."

effects.log: You sit up with them. It is quiet. You have not done this as often as you ought to.

events.text: You were the one who sent {elu_m}. You know that. {em_He} knew that, too, on the way out of the gate, and made a joke about it. It was not a very good joke. You have remembered it several times today. The others are waiting, in the yard, for you to come down and be the person who knows what to do.

choices.text: Go down

effects.log: You go down. You know what to do; you have done it before. It is the worst thing about the whole business.

choices.text: Let the second-in-line do it, this once

effects.log: They look up at your window, and then they do it themselves, rather well. You will have to think about that.

events.text: A stranger has brought you the news of {elu_m} along with the sum of {em_his} savings, which was {em_his} wish, it seems. It is a very small purse, with a note on who it should go to: {elu_the}, for wine, on the day of the next thing that goes wrong. You have just been told a good deal, about what {em_he} expected of you all.

choices.text: Keep the purse for the next bad day

effects.log: It sits on the shelf. When the day comes, there is a dreadful wine, and nobody can drink it, and they all do.

choices.text: Open it tonight

effects.log: It is a bad day, you tell them. They do not argue. It is an extremely bad wine.

events.text: With {elu_m} gone there is no one to give orders in {elu_the} when you are not looking. The oldest thinks it should be the oldest. The best thinks it should be the best. {elu_m} would have had something to say on this and it would have been unkind. They are all looking at you now.

choices.text: Choose the one who has not asked

effects.log: They are horrified. They accept. Within a year you cannot imagine how you ever thought of anyone else.

choices.text: Choose the best of them

effects.log: It is the obvious choice, and it is a good one, and there is a certain amount of slamming doors.

events.text: Nobody has been sleeping in the captain's bunk, and {elu_the} are getting odd about it. Somebody leaves it flowers, and somebody moves the flowers. In the end you walk in and sit on it yourself, and ask them all which of them you would have to tell off for this.

choices.text: Promote the one who laughs

effects.log: It is the right call, for no reason you could explain to a council. The bunk has someone in it by nightfall.

choices.text: Promote the one who moved the flowers

effects.log: It takes them a moment to realise you knew. The new captain turns red, and then does extremely well.

events.text: At a gathering in the provincial capital, the people at the next table are {elu_rv}, every one of them famous. Their captain, {elu_rvc}, looks over and raises a cup. {elu_way} {elu_m} has gone stiff next to you. "They have heard of us," {em_he} says, and you can hear {em_him} trying not to be pleased.

choices.text: Raise your cup back

effects.log: It is very civil. Afterwards, you cannot get {elu_the} to stop talking about what they would have done differently.

choices.text: Walk over and introduce yourself

effects.log: {elu_rvc} has a firm grip and a very good memory. "We will meet," is about all that gets said, and it gets said pleasantly.

events.text: Some enterprising person has started selling woodcuts of famous fighting companies at the markets. There are six in the set. {elu_rv} is on the front. {elu_The} are not in it at all. {elu_m} has bought one anyway and has pinned it up in the barracks, with a note on it, in {em_his} hand, about what they do wrong with their left flank.

choices.text: Leave it up

effects.log: It stays up. There are soon several notes in different hands. It becomes the most-studied document you own.

choices.text: Send the set to {elu_rvc}, with the notes

effects.log: You get it back within the season. There are new notes on it. They are correct, and they are about you.

events.text: {elu_rvc} has come to see you, in plain clothes, without any of {elu_rv}, and has brought good tea. It is a courtesy call. {elu_way} They sit in your hall drinking and asking after your health, and they know exactly how many of your people are in the building. You know that they know. It is a very pleasant afternoon.

choices.text: Return the courtesy, next spring

effects.log: You go. You drink their tea, and you count their people. Nobody is in any doubt about what this is. In a way, it is the most honest friendship you have.

choices.text: Have {elu_m} walk them to the gate

effects.log: {elu_m} says nothing all the way down. {elu_rvc} remarks that it was a nice walk, and nods to {em_him} at parting, as to someone they will know again.

events.text: It was bound to happen. {elu_The} and {elu_rv} have reached the same bridge from different sides on the same morning, on errands that cannot both be done. {elu_rvc} rides forward. So does {elu_m}. Neither of them has drawn. "After you," {elu_rvc} says, and {em_he} looks back to you to see what you meant by this.

choices.text: Tell {elu_m} to take the bridge

effects.log: It is over in the time it takes to boil rice, and everyone will be telling it wrong by nightfall.

choices.text: Propose it be settled with one bout each

effects.log: Three bouts, on the bridge, with both sides watching and shouting advice. It is the best thing anyone has seen all year.

events.text: There is a contract out on the salt road, and the great houses have all been told about it. {elu_rv} will have it unless somebody takes it from them. It would be a matter of being there first, or of being better. {elu_m} has been over the ground. {em_He} thinks the two companies will see each other at the second ford.

choices.text: Race them there, and hold it

effects.log: You send them at a dead run. There is a great deal of mud, and it gets settled in the mud.

choices.text: Let them get there first, then outdo them

effects.log: It is the harder way. Let them have the ford, you say, and do the job better. {elu_m} looks pained, and gets on with it.

events.text: At the Autumn Gathering they let two companies show their drill on the great floor before the elders of nine sects. It is supposed to be friendly. There are seven hundred people watching, a lot of them with money riding on it. {elu_rvc} bows from across the floor. {elu_m} has been sick twice this morning and says that it means nothing.

choices.text: Tell them to go for the throat

effects.log: It stops being a drill at about the third pass, and nobody on the floor minds. The physicians are kept busy.

choices.text: Tell them: clean, correct, no mistakes

effects.log: They perform it as if nobody were there. It is very beautiful. Only those who have done this for a living can see how close it is.

events.text: Three of {elu_rv} were caught in a pass by the snow, in a bad way, and it was your people who found them. {elu_m} sends to ask what you want done. Those three know the routes and the numbers of the whole company, and they are very cold. {elu_m} adds, in a postscript, that {em_he} has already lit the fire, whatever you decide.

choices.text: Hold them, and make them talk

effects.log: They talk, eventually, in between the soup. You have everything you need for next time. {elu_rvc} sends a very short note.

choices.text: Feed them, and send them home

effects.log: They go home with your people's coats on. {elu_rvc} sends the coats back, cleaned, with a note, and you are all a little embarrassed.

events.text: A very good offer has reached {elu_m}, from {elu_rv}: more silver, a better rank and a house near the sea. {em_He} has shown it to you, which is the correct thing to do, and now {em_he} is waiting. You have noticed that the letter has been folded and unfolded quite a few times.

choices.text: Match it, and more

effects.log: It is a lot of silver, and it is the only language you are sure of. {elu_m} takes it. Both of you pretend it was about the silver.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} that it is up to {em_him}

effects.log: You do not say anything else. {em_He} folds the letter again, and in the morning it is in the kitchen fire, and {em_he} is out in the yard. Probably. You check the fire.

choices.text: "Go, if you are going."

effects.log: You say it too quickly. {em_He} bows. {elu_rv} get a fine new blade, and {elu_rvc} sends a basket of fruit.

events.text: {elu_rvc} has written to you directly. They would like to borrow {elu_m}, for a season, to teach their juniors one particular thing that {em_he} does on a stair. It is a compliment and a raid at the same time, and there is nothing in the customs of the martial world that lets you say so.

choices.text: Lend {em_him}, and ask for one of theirs

effects.log: It turns into an exchange. Everyone learns something. Everyone is very careful about what they teach.

choices.text: Refuse politely

effects.log: You refuse politely. {elu_rvc} replies politely. {elu_m} finds out, and is rather flattered, and is out on the stairs practising.

events.text: They come to you with their banner rolled. It has been a long rivalry, and {elu_rvc} is older now. Nobody has quite said that {elu_the} have won. It is just that at all the great gatherings, people now look at your people first. {elu_rvc} sits down and takes a cup, and says: "Next time you see those youngsters of ours, go easy. No. Do not."

choices.text: Offer a toast to {elu_rv}

effects.log: You raise your cup to them, and mean it. There are not many people left who know what that was worth, and you are both sitting at this table.

choices.text: Ask them for the woodcut

effects.log: {elu_rvc} laughs until someone has to bring water. It arrives in the post a month later, with your people on the front.

events.text: The story is all over the province: at last, {elu_the} have the better of {elu_rv}. {elu_m} has had to stop three people from having a parade. {elu_The} look at you with something like suspicion: what happens to you, now that you have got what you wanted? You had not thought about that either.

choices.text: Find them someone worse

effects.log: You always can. It takes a season or two. {elu_m} is much happier, and so, you notice, are you.

choices.text: Give them a whole month off

effects.log: Nobody knows what to do. Several of them turn up at the drill anyway. One of them learns to fish, and is terrible at it.

events.text: Nobody says it, but it is settled: {elu_rv} are the better company, and everyone knows it, and {elu_rvc} has had the grace not to mention it in front of you. {elu_m} has been doing the accounts of the bouts, won and lost, and now closes the book. "We are good," {em_he} says. "It is a very annoying thing to be, next to them."

choices.text: Ask {elu_rvc} to teach you what you missed

effects.log: It takes all your pride, and one long lunch. {elu_rvc} tells you everything, because you asked, and you are better for it.

choices.text: Tell them it is only a matter of time

effects.log: It is not really true. It is what they need to hear, and it gets them up at dawn.

events.text: {elu_rv} have taken the field at the great muster, and you have been given a place on their left, as an auxiliary. It is an honour. It says so on the invitation. {elu_The} line up in very good order and very bad temper, while {elu_rvc} goes past them on a tall horse and salutes, quite correctly, the way one salutes the auxiliaries.

choices.text: Salute back, smiling

effects.log: It costs a great deal, and it is seen by everyone who matters. They will remember the smile longer than the placement.

choices.text: Have them march off the field

effects.log: It is magnificent, and it makes you no friends at all, and {elu_rvc}, watching, is seen to nod.

events.text: The elders of the house have noticed that the person sitting in its chair, who was not born to it, now keeps a squad with its own name and its own wages. {elu_The} were raised with your own silver. A senior aunt invites you to tea and asks, very gently, who exactly it is they are for.

choices.text: Offer to send half of them home

effects.log: She is pleased. She had not expected you to give up so much, she says. She takes note of which half you kept.

choices.text: "They are for me, Aunt."

effects.log: She sets down her cup without a sound. "Yes," she says. "We had thought so." The house has been very polite to you since.

choices.text: Swear them to the house's tablets

effects.log: It takes an afternoon and some bowing. They are a little less yours, on paper. The aunts go back to their embroidery.

events.text: One of the house's own guard came to you last night, in the dark, to tell you that the elders have put a watcher into {elu_the}. They did not know which of them it was. They wanted you to know that they were sorry about it. The house has always done this to people like you, it seems, and they have always done it to people they respected.

choices.text: Thin out the list, quietly

effects.log: You send two away on long errands, and the talk dies down. You still do not know whether you sent away the right ones.

choices.text: Announce it at the house's dinner

effects.log: You stand up with your cup and thank the elders for their concern. There are a lot of people who suddenly need to look at their soup.

events.text: The house has its own company, and has had for two hundred years, and it has not failed to notice yours. Word comes down from the back rooms that a good head of the family would naturally merge the two, with the old company's captain in charge. It is put to you as an honour.

choices.text: Agree, and keep your own captain as deputy

effects.log: You have been outmanoeuvred, a little, and you have managed it with style. You have someone on the inside of the old company now.

choices.text: Decline, with the deepest respect

effects.log: They receive it with the deepest respect. Your tea at the next family dinner is cold.

events.text: You have never said it would be this year. {elu_The} have simply started to know their way around the corridors of the head of the house, in soft shoes, by a good many doors you never mentioned. {elu_m} has been holding your outer coat at some odd moments. "Whatever you do in there, one of these days," {em_he} says, "nobody is coming through that door behind you."

choices.text: "Nobody dies who does not draw."

effects.log: {elu_m} passes it along the line. Whatever comes of it, they will say that you said that.

choices.text: Say nothing, and go on walking

effects.log: There is nothing to say. Behind you, you hear {elu_m} try the handle of a door, in a thoughtful way.

events.text: You are a guest in this house and you have been a good one for years. But there are people of yours who have been drinking in the same three taverns as the guards of this house for a very long time, and lately those guards have been losing a good deal of sleep to a card game. You recognise the hand of {elu_m} in this, and you have not asked about it.

choices.text: Thank {em_him}, briefly

effects.log: "For what?" {elu_m} says, and looks at the sky. It is an excellent night for cards.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to pull them back if it goes badly

effects.log: {elu_m} looks at you as if you have said something in a foreign language. "Of course," {em_he} says. {em_He} plainly has no plans to.

events.text: You no longer hold the seat that {elu_the} were sworn under. The new order has sent you a very correct letter, with a list. It says that a unit of this name is carried on its rolls, and asks when they may expect to receive it. {elu_m} has read it over your shoulder. {em_He} has stopped pretending not to.

choices.text: Release them. They were the seat's

effects.log: You go down and tell them. It is quite short. They march out in good order, and the name goes on after you, in other hands. It is in the chronicle, and it has your name beside it.

choices.text: Ask who wants to come with you

effects.log: It is not everyone. It is enough, for a small band on the road, and now it will cost you. They were the seat's, and the seat will remember this.

choices.text: Stand them down, and break the banner

effects.log: You will not see it carried by anyone else. They look at you and they do as you say, and go their ways. Nobody takes the name again.

events.text: It all happened quickly, as these things do. You have your things in a cart. There are people at the gate who are extremely sorry to have to check the cart. Then, from the barracks, {elu_m} comes walking across the yard in full kit with a bedroll over {em_his} shoulder, followed by several more, none of them looking at the people at the gate.

choices.text: "You will lose your pensions."

effects.log: "Yes," {elu_m} says, and puts {em_his} bedroll in the cart.

choices.text: Send them back

effects.log: You tell them to go back, and you make it an order. It is the last one. {elu_m} stands there a moment, and salutes, and {elu_the} stay on, under another hand.

events.text: You handed it on properly, with a ceremony and a good speech, and it was only afterwards anyone thought of asking who {elu_the} now answer to. Your successor would be delighted to keep them. Your successor also would like it known that {elu_m} has a way of looking at them in the yard, and asks whether you could have a word.

choices.text: Tell {elu_m} to serve your successor as they served you

effects.log: {elu_m} looks at you for a good while. "That is an order?" "It is." They serve. It is not the same, and you do not visit the yard.

choices.text: Take them with you, as a personal guard

effects.log: Your successor is very gracious about it, and very relieved. A retired head with their own company is the talk of the province for years.

choices.text: Disband them, with honours

effects.log: There is a dinner. There are speeches. The banner is put away in the hall, where it will gather dust and be pointed out to visitors.

events.text: They have read out the charges against you, and they have taken the seat. It is all very regular. {elu_The} have been told they are under new orders as of this morning. When you are walked across the yard, you see that every one of them has turned out, in full order, and that they do not salute anyone else.

choices.text: Shake your head at {elu_m}

effects.log: A very small movement. {elu_m} sees it. They stay where they are. It is the best order you ever gave them, and it hurts a good deal.

choices.text: Nod

effects.log: It is a very small movement. By the next morning there is a good deal less of the old guard in the barracks, and a small company has been seen on the river road.

events.text: You have the seat now, and with it you have {elu_the}: a company that swore an oath to someone you buried last month. {elu_m} has come to ask, in the plainest possible words, whether the oath still stands or whether they should look for work. Behind {em_him} there are a lot of people you have known since you were small, and they are all standing very straight.

choices.text: "Swear it again. To me, this time."

effects.log: They do it in the same yard, in the same words. A few of them have to stop for a moment.

choices.text: "You owe me nothing. Stay if you like."

effects.log: It is very quiet. Nobody goes. Later you find that it has done more than an oath would.

events.text: Your parent's people have a way of comparing you, and they do not know they are doing it. {elu_m} calls you by the old title once, by accident, and goes white. {elu_The} are the finest thing you have been left, and the most difficult. There is a good case for replacing the older ones with your own.

choices.text: Keep them all, and put up with it
