effects.log: It will take a decade before they stop looking over your shoulder for someone. By then, you will have started doing it yourself.

choices.text: Retire the oldest, gently, and bring in your own

effects.log: There is a dinner, and some good silver. {elu_The} are younger now, and quicker, and a few things only the old ones knew are gone.

events.text: Nobody told you this: there is a page in the unit's rolls, in your parent's hand, about you. {elu_m} has been keeping it, and has brought it to you without comment. It lists what you are bad at. It is very accurate, and it ends: "They will have to find out for themselves. Help them, and do not let them see."

choices.text: Thank {elu_m}, and ask how long it has been helping

effects.log: "Since you were twelve," {elu_m} says. A number of things about your childhood become clearer.

choices.text: Put it back in the rolls without a word

effects.log: {elu_m} says nothing either. In the morning somebody has added a line under it: "Starting to."

events.text: A company with no seat behind it has to eat. {elu_The} have taken to guarding things for people who are not sure they can afford it. {elu_m} has sold a very good horse to pay for the winter, and has not told you, and you know because there is one fewer horse. There is talk of what it would take to get something of your own again.

choices.text: Sell something of your own

effects.log: You do it where they can see. There is less talk now, and people sit nearer the fire.

choices.text: Tell them to find work, and you will call them

effects.log: They find work. They are very good, and they send you a share you did not ask for. They do come back.

events.text: It has been some years. There is an old soldier with a bad back in an inn on the road who was at the gate the day you left, and who says everyone there is sorry now. {elu_m} thinks this is the moment. {elu_The} are few, and old, and they would follow you back up that road for a bowl of rice and a chance to shout at somebody.

choices.text: Not yet. Keep them ready

effects.log: They nod. They go on being ready. It is what they are best at, and there is something to be said for it.

choices.text: Tell them it is over

effects.log: You have been meaning to say so for a while. They hear you out. They do not leave. It seems you do not get a vote.

events.text: You have put {elu_m} into {elu_the}, on top of the rank you already gave {em_him} faster than the rules ask. The hall had just about finished talking about that. The squad has now begun. Nobody says a word in {em_his} hearing. Somebody has simply left an extra bowl at the table, labelled "for {em_his} patron."

choices.text: Sit down and eat from it

effects.log: You eat every grain, in front of them. {elu_m} sits next to you and is very red. The bowl does not appear again.

choices.text: Send {em_him} first on the next hard job

effects.log: If {em_he} comes back, nobody will be talking about bowls. {elu_m} knows exactly what you are doing, and says thank you.

events.text: The old hands of {elu_the} have asked to see you, all together, with their helmets under their arms. They have no complaint about {elu_m}. {em_He} is a fine young person. They would only like to know which of them is expected to take orders from a rank that came so quickly, and they can wait for your answer as long as it takes.

choices.text: "None of you. In this unit, rank stops at the door."

effects.log: It is a rule you have just invented. It goes on to outlive you, and {elu_m} has to earn every step here all over again.

choices.text: "Test {em_him}, then."

effects.log: They test {em_him} for a whole season, and it is not nice. There is grudging respect by the end of it, or at least fewer bruises.

events.text: Pay-day came and went. {elu_The} have not said a word, and that is the alarming part. {elu_m} has brought you the accounts, open, and has set them down with no comment. Three of them have started doing odd jobs in town. You have seen one of the finest blades in the province mending a fence.

choices.text: Sell something, and pay them

effects.log: It hurts. They get paid. The fence is finished by someone else, and rather worse.

choices.text: Tell them the truth, and ask them to wait

effects.log: You stand up and say so. They hear you out. They will wait. It will be remembered, and in both directions.

events.text: A creditor has come to your door with a list of what {elu_the} owe in town: boots, wine, a window. {elu_m} would like it known that the window was justified. Nobody has seen wages in a long while, and now the town has started to be careful of them, which is a thing you had hoped never to see.

choices.text: Settle the whole list

effects.log: The town breathes out. So does {elu_m}. Your purse does not.

choices.text: Have {elu_m} deal with the creditor

effects.log: It is settled, and you never hear how. Nobody in town mentions the window again. They do not mention much at all.

events.text: You walk through the barracks of {elu_the} and see that you do not know who half of them are. The new ones are very young. They stand up very fast when you come in, as they would for a shrine. The drill has changed in ways nobody decided. On the wall, the banner is the third one, and somebody has had the first one framed.

choices.text: Learn every name by the end of the month

effects.log: You do it. It is not as easy as it used to be. A few of them are the grandchildren of people you buried.

choices.text: Let them have their own captains now

effects.log: They do not need you in the barracks. You had known that for some time, and you take your hands off the rail.

events.text: {elu_m} is teaching the recruits a song about {elu_the}. You have never heard it before. It is about you, supposedly, and it has you winning a battle that you remember rather differently, on a day when you mainly remember being sick. It is quite catchy. You catch yourself humming it on the stairs.

choices.text: Correct the verses

effects.log: They listen with respect, and go on singing the old ones. Nobody wants a true song about being sick.

choices.text: Teach them a worse one

effects.log: You knew some terrible ones, in your day. There is a great deal of delighted shock in the barracks. It is the first time they have thought of you as a person.

events.text: A recruit asks who the empty place at the end of the table is for. There have been so many people, and the custom is older than anyone at the table but you. You look along it and find that you are the only one left who knows the answer, and that the answer is a name, and that you almost did not have it.

choices.text: Tell them, and tell them all of it

effects.log: It takes the whole evening. They are very quiet. You have them write it down.

choices.text: Tell them it is for whoever comes next

effects.log: It is not the truth, or not the first truth. It will do, for them. You remember the name for yourself, on the stairs.

events.text: Someone at court has asked to see the rolls of {elu_the}, for a history. It has been a good long while since anyone counted. The clerk who comes back with the sum looks at you differently. There are a good many battles there. He would like to know whether it is true about the bridge.

choices.text: "Which bridge?"

effects.log: He laughs. Then he sees that you are serious, and takes out his brush again.

choices.text: "Put in the ones we lost, too"

effects.log: It makes for a longer book. It is the only one on the shelf that anybody trusts.

events.text: They are using the name in the markets now, to sell boots. "As worn by." You have had a representative of {elu_the} look into it, and {elu_m} has come back wearing a pair. They are excellent boots. There is a story in the provinces that if you say the name three times on a bad road, you will get home.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: It costs nothing. A few people do get home. You could not say what that has to do with you.

choices.text: Send a few of them to walk that road

effects.log: After that, it is not quite a story. It is good for the boots.

events.text: A very old enemy, on the last day of a long truce, sends you one line: "I have fought all of you, and I wish you had been on my side, and I am glad you were not." {elu_m} reads it, and asks if {em_he} can have it for the unit. It goes up in the mess hall beside the bad banner.

choices.text: Send one line back

effects.log: You think for a week. You write: "So do we." Nobody knows whether it ever arrived.

choices.text: Say nothing, and drink to the old enemy

effects.log: They all drink. The younger ones want to know who it was, and the old ones begin, and it goes on for some time.

events.text: There is an old fellow at an inn on the road, telling a story to some children, and it takes you a moment to catch it. It is about a company called {elu_old}. He has most of it wrong. You find you know which parts, and you have never heard the name before in this life. You have gone cold, and you do not know why, and you tip him rather too much.

choices.text: Ask what became of them

effects.log: He has an ending, and it is a good one, and you are nearly sure that it is not true. You go on your way a little more slowly.

choices.text: Finish your soup

effects.log: You finish it. It does not taste of very much. You catch yourself humming, later, on the road, something that you could not have learned.

events.text: In a provincial armoury they keep a piece of old banner under glass, as they do. It is badly sewn. The label says {elu_old}, "date uncertain". The keeper is delighted that anyone has stopped to look. You find you know, for no reason, exactly where the crooked stitch is going to be, before you get round to that side.

choices.text: Ask to hold it

effects.log: The keeper looks shocked, and then lets you. It weighs almost nothing. Someone made it very badly, and with great care.

choices.text: Tell the keeper the label is wrong

effects.log: "Is it?" says the keeper, reaching for a pen. You have no idea what to say. You leave rather quickly.

events.text: Somebody at the next table says that a fellow is as stubborn as {elu_old}. You ask who that was. Nobody knows. It is just a saying around here, they tell you. It has apparently been one for longer than the inn has stood. You go on eating, and you find your hand has gone to a place at your left side, where nobody is standing.

choices.text: Drink to them, whoever they were

effects.log: The table is happy to oblige. They drink to a lot of things. It feels like paying a very small part of a very large debt.

choices.text: Let it pass

effects.log: You let it pass. It is only a saying. It is a long way home from here, and you do not know why you thought so.

events.text: {elu_rv} are the pride of your own house, and they do not take applications. An old captain has been watching you at the morning drill for a month, and today {elu_rvc} has stopped beside you and asked to see your wrist, as one looks at a horse. {elu_way} It would mean more merit and much less sleep, for a season or two.

choices.text: Accept the season

effects.log: You spend it being shouted at by the finest people you have ever met. You will be dining out on this for years.

choices.text: Decline, politely

effects.log: {elu_rvc} shrugs. There are others. You do notice they keep an eye on you, now and then, in the yard.

events.text: The famous {elu_rv} are short of a body for a job this spring, and you were standing nearest. {elu_rvc} would like you to understand this is not an honour. You are to carry things, keep quiet and stay out of the way of anyone who knows what they are doing. A good many people in your position have started this way.

choices.text: Carry things

effects.log: You carry a very great number of things. You also get to see how it is really done, from about six feet away.

choices.text: Say you have work of your own

effects.log: {elu_rvc} gives you a long look and says that this is a fine answer, and that nobody is likely to ask you again.

events.text: Your isle is small and the winds around it are not. You call together the immortals who came up the white stairs to you, each of them with a few centuries of bad habits, and tell them that from today some of them will be {elu_name}. The eldest wants to know whether the title carries a Register number at the Jade Court. Of course it does. Everything does.

choices.text: File it with the Court, in full

effects.log: It takes eleven years for the stamp to come back, which is quick up here. It is a very handsome stamp.

choices.text: Leave the Court out of it

effects.log: No clerk knows of them. Your rivals on the Isles find this unsettling, as you hoped.

events.text: A sword immortal who has not spoken in sixty years comes to the edge of your isle and looks at the drop. "Will there be walking," the sword immortal says at last. You say there will be flying, and fighting, and a banner that says {elu_name}. A long pause. "Walking was better." Then that one goes and gets the others.

choices.text: Let them keep their silences

effects.log: You have the quietest company above the clouds, and the worst at taking messages.

choices.text: Make them talk at supper

effects.log: It is excruciating. It takes twenty years. It does help, in a fight, to know what your neighbour hates.

events.text: The Eight Houses keep their guards in lacquer, and you have only your own line. You stand your kin along the cloud-terrace, those with the sword in them and those who at least will not fall off, and you name them {elu_name}. A grand-niece of four hundred asks if there will be matching robes, and you discover there is budget for one robe.

choices.text: Give the robe to the worst of them

effects.log: They wear it as if it were armour, and in time it more or less is.

choices.text: Hang it on the terrace, as a banner

effects.log: It flaps at a great height. Other Houses ask what it means. So do you, on some mornings.

events.text: A house above the clouds lasts as long as the people who would die for it, and up here nobody has to die of anything except each other. You have seen what the great lines keep behind their screens. Now your own line has something of the kind, and its name is {elu_name}. Your eldest kin bows and asks who is going to tell the other seven houses.

choices.text: Tell the go-betweens first

effects.log: There is an immediate improvement in the quality of your in-laws, and in how carefully they speak to you.

choices.text: Tell nobody yet

effects.log: A house that hides its blade is at least a house with a blade to hide. They train under the clouds, in the rain.

events.text: They give you a Cloud Legion's worth of rank and a Legion's worth of paperwork, and nobody ever said you could not pick your own. You go along the cloud-barges reading names, looking for those with old scars and bad records. {elu_name}, you write at the head of the page, and you send it up to the Ministry of War, where it may be read in a century.

choices.text: Attach a very polite note

effects.log: The note goes up with the page. It is the only reason anybody at the Ministry remembers your name, in the end.

choices.text: Do not wait for the answer

effects.log: They are in the field by the time the first clerk has found the right form. It is, technically, a crime. It is also rather usual.

events.text: You have climbed high enough in your faction that your orders are now obeyed by people who think you are wrong. It seems wise to keep a few who think you are right, close by. So, on a cloud-barge going nowhere, over very bad tea, you ask them. They are {elu_name} by the time the pot is empty, and no one wrote any of it down.

choices.text: Write it down

effects.log: It is not a long list. You keep it in your sleeve for a few hundred years, and it wears thin along the folds.

choices.text: Burn the tea leaves, for luck

effects.log: It is an old cloud-barge custom. Nobody can say what it means. It does not seem to hurt.

events.text: A cloud-barge full of Isle herbs has gone missing between two chains, and the Jade Court has not been able to find it in nine years. {elu_m} suggests that {elu_the} might. It would be a fine way to be noticed, and it would be noticed by whoever is growing rich on those herbs now.

choices.text: Go and find it

effects.log: They find it in a very odd place, with a very odd crew. There are a good many apologies from people who outrank you.

choices.text: Go and find who wants it found

effects.log: Nine years is a long time for a barge to stay lost. You learn more from who is asking than from the barge.

events.text: A cloud-barge of the Jade Court must cross the Sundered Reach this century, and the Reach has a way of keeping what crosses it. {elu_m} has read all the old manifests, which is more than the Court did. {elu_The} can sail high in full array, for all the Isles to see, or low in the weather, where nobody looks.

choices.text: High, in full array

effects.log: Let the Isles count them. {elu_m} sends for the good robes.

choices.text: Low, in the weather

effects.log: It will be wet and slow, and {elu_m} seems content with that.

events.text: A minister's very young daughter, who is six hundred, is to travel to the Star Sea to study, and she has eluded three escorts so far. {elu_m} has been asked to see that she arrives. {em_He} has asked whether that means with her consent.

choices.text: Without it: stay on her heels

effects.log: It will be the most exhausting century {elu_m} has ever known.

choices.text: With it: make friends

effects.log: {elu_m} goes to tea, and takes along the one who is good at cards.

events.text: A rival on the next chain has stopped paying its dues in spirit stones and has started, very quietly, moving its boundary markers across the open cloud. There is nothing the Rolls can do about a thing that drifts. {elu_m} asks whether {elu_the} should also start to drift.

choices.text: Take their isle's lower terrace, in daylight

effects.log: It is an act of open war, by the standards of anyone who has not been at it for ten thousand years.

choices.text: Cut their markers loose, by night

effects.log: They will wake up somewhere else. {elu_m} seems to enjoy this more than is proper.

events.text: A faction's treasure-grotto has lain open since its warden went to sleep two thousand years ago. Everyone has agreed not to notice, because everyone is afraid of who else might. {elu_m} has noticed. {em_He} has a list of what is inside it and a list of who would object.

choices.text: Empty it, and leave your name

effects.log: Someone had to be first. {elu_m} takes a great many bags.

choices.text: Take a single thing, and put back the dust

effects.log: A single thing. {elu_m} goes in with a very small brush.

events.text: The Rolls of the Jade Court are not secret. They are merely in nine hundred thousand volumes, in an order that only three clerks understand, and one of those three has started to take a drink with {elu_m}. Somebody has entered your name under a heading you would like to read.

choices.text: Break in, and read it

effects.log: The stacks are guarded by things that were clerks once. {elu_m} takes a lamp and a sword.

choices.text: Keep buying the drinks

effects.log: It may take decades. {elu_m} has started to enjoy the clerk's company, a good deal more than the wine.

events.text: A Cloud-Veil has walked through your isle twice this decade: someone from above you, wearing the seeming of nobody at all. It only fools those below them, so it must be someone who has decided that you are below them. {elu_m} can feel where they stand, or says so. {em_He} would like to know how much you want to learn.

choices.text: Lay a snare at the stair

effects.log: A person who thinks nobody can see them makes mistakes. So does a person laying a snare for such a person.

choices.text: Watch, and let them come again

effects.log: {elu_m} sits up with the wind. Your isle is very polite to nobody at all, for some years.

events.text: Two factions have begun to fight over the Reach, as they do each few centuries, and the Heavens are full of sails. {elu_foe} has made it clear that no neutral isle will be left so. {elu_m} has already had {elu_the} sharpening things, in case you would like to have a say in how this is told in the next Rolls.

choices.text: Send them in where it is thickest

effects.log: A few of them get a mention in the Rolls. That is more than the rest of the sky will get.

choices.text: Hold your own isle and let nobody land

effects.log: Nobody lands. It will be a hundred years before anyone is very friendly to you.

choices.text: Sit this one out

effects.log: You take a very long view of it. {elu_m} takes a very long view of you.

events.text: It is a war of the sort only immortals have, and it has been going on since before you came up the white stairs. Nobody remembers the cause. {elu_foe} sends a herald each decade to ask if you will finally choose. {elu_m} says that this time the herald has brought an actual army.

choices.text: Meet it on the open cloud

effects.log: You had almost forgotten what this was like. So had {elu_foe}.

choices.text: Fall back to the stone

effects.log: The isle takes the blows. It has taken worse, and it says so, by creaking.

events.text: {elu_m} does not look down. You had taken that for pride, until the day you see {em_him} cross the bridge between two terraces with {em_his} eyes shut and {em_his} jaw set. An immortal of eight centuries, afraid of the drop, in a realm that is all drop. {em_He} sees you see it. "Say one word," {em_he} says, "and I shall have to duel you."

choices.text: Say nothing, and walk on the outside

effects.log: From then on, you happen to walk on the outside of every bridge. Neither of you ever mentions it.

choices.text: Say: "I was afraid of it too"

effects.log: It is not quite true. {em_He} snorts, and takes a long time to answer, and that evening {em_he} tells you how it began.

events.text: The thing {elu_m} is afraid of is below. It is not the drop; it is what is at the bottom of it. {em_He} left a village down there, eight hundred years ago, with a promise to come back. {em_He} has worked out how long a village lasts. There is a Descend coming up on the Rolls, and {em_he} has asked you, very stiffly, if a member of {elu_the} might be permitted to go.

choices.text: Let {em_him} go down and look

effects.log: It costs you a good blade for a decade. {em_He} comes back with a handful of ordinary soil, and looks over the edge at last.

choices.text: You need {em_him} here

effects.log: {em_He} bows. {em_He} goes back to not looking. You catch {em_him} at it sometimes, at the very edge.

events.text: In a fight off the Reach, the terrace goes, and with it the bridge, and there is nothing under {elu_m} but all that air. You see it from across the gap. {em_He} looks down, at last, and {em_his} face changes. {em_He} could get back to you, perhaps. There is also someone below {em_him}, one of the young ones, who has already started to fall.

choices.text: Shout at {em_him} to come back to you

effects.log: You shout. {em_He} looks up, and comes, the long way, furious, with the young one over {em_his} shoulder, and never again keeps {em_his} eyes shut. {em_He} is the first on every bridge now.

choices.text: Keep your mouth shut, and let {em_him} choose

effects.log: {em_He} steps off. {em_He} goes down after the young one very fast, with {em_his} eyes open. The young one comes back. {em_He} does not; the sky is big.

events.text: {elu_m} has been carrying on a grudge for eleven thousand years against someone in {elu_rv}. Nobody remembers what about, including, it seems, {elu_m}. It takes up about a tenth of {em_his} time. {em_He} sends a rude letter every century, and receives one, and has started to file them.

choices.text: Ask to read the file

effects.log: It is a remarkable document, and very funny, and rather sad in the middle. {em_He} seems pleased that somebody asked.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to let it go

effects.log: {em_He} looks at you as if you had suggested {em_he} let go of {em_his} legs.

events.text: This century the letter has not come. {elu_m} has been to the barge landing every morning for a year. {em_He} says that it is nothing, that the post is slow up here, that {em_he} never cared in the least. {em_He} is not sleeping. There is a rumour out of {elu_rv} that an old immortal among them has started to forget things.

choices.text: Send {em_him} to find out

effects.log: {em_He} goes off to be rude to the person in person. {em_He} is gone for a very long time, for {em_him}.

choices.text: Write a letter yourself, in {em_his} style

effects.log: It is a bad forgery. An answer comes, in a shaky hand, correcting your insults. {elu_m} does not say anything for a while.

events.text: {elu_m} is back. {em_He} has brought with {em_him} a very old person from {elu_rv}, who has no idea where they are and is quite cheerful about it, and keeps asking who this rude young fellow might be. "I am going to have to explain the whole thing to them," {elu_m} says. "From the beginning. It will take about a thousand years. I would like to ask for leave."

choices.text: Give {em_him} leave, for as long as it takes

effects.log: They take the small house on the windward side. You can hear them in there arguing, on good days. {elu_m} does not come back to the line, and {em_he} is happier than you have ever seen.

choices.text: Give them both a room, and keep {em_him} on the rolls

effects.log: It is very irregular. {elu_rv} send a stiff letter of thanks. {elu_m} fights better than {em_he} has in an age, and has someone to report to at the end of it.

events.text: Word has come to you through someone well-placed that a charge is being got ready for the Rolls, and that its witnesses are to be your own people. {elu_m} has been asked, very respectfully, to recall certain events. There is a Cloud-Veil at the bottom of it, you are told: one of those above you, seeming to be a clerk.

choices.text: Tell {elu_m} to recall whatever {em_he} likes

effects.log: You have said it to {em_his} face. {em_He} recalls, in the event, nothing at all, to anyone, and in very great detail.

choices.text: Have them all make false statements, and see which leak

effects.log: The Rolls are full of it for years. You find your leak. Your people find out how you found it.

events.text: They have offered {elu_m} a Ministry. It is not a small one. {em_He} would have a seat at the Jade Court and an isle of {em_his} own, and all {em_he} has to do is stop being with you on a day {em_he} will be told about later. {em_He} has come to report it, and has mentioned, in passing, what the view is like.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to take the post, and report to you

effects.log: Now you have a minister. For a while, at any rate. {elu_m} looks at you with a certain interest as {em_he} goes.

choices.text: Say you would hate to stand in the way of that view

effects.log: A long silence. "It is not such a good view," {elu_m} says, at last, and {em_he} is at the drill next morning.

events.text: An immortal who dies leaves very little. {elu_m} left a stain on the cloud that the wind has been working on for a week, and a list of debts going back several thousand years, all of them paid. {elu_The} stand along the terrace. Nobody up here has much practice at this. It is the thing you came up the white stairs to stop having to do.

choices.text: Enter the name on the Rolls yourself

effects.log: You stand in line for it, for a week, as anyone must. The clerk looks up when you give the name, and says that it was a good one.

choices.text: Keep the list

effects.log: You read through all of it. Quite a lot of it is people you know, and all of it was settled. You think about your own for some time.

events.text: It has been a hundred years and {elu_m} has not come back from the Reach. Up here, that does not have to mean anything. {elu_The} go on sending out a barge, each decade, to look. They have asked you whether it is time to stop, and they ask very carefully, in the voice of those who have outlived a great many people and do not want to do it again.

choices.text: Send one more barge

effects.log: You send one more, and then, after a decade, one more. It is not a great expense. You do not intend to be the one who says.

choices.text: Let them turn the bowl over

effects.log: You give the order. It takes them a day to do it. The sky goes on being very large.

events.text: At the Heavenly Calendar's great gathering, the sails of {elu_rv} are moored next to yours, and their captain, {elu_rvc}, has crossed over to look at your rigging. {elu_way} It is a long-lived sort of courtesy. It will be some centuries before you know what it meant. {elu_m} is watching from the rail, without blinking.

choices.text: Offer the stool, and the bad tea

effects.log: You pass a pleasant hour. {elu_rvc} remarks that your people hold their blades too high. They are correct.

choices.text: Have a look at their rigging

effects.log: {elu_rvc} is delighted. You get quite a thorough tour, of the parts they want you to see.

events.text: There is a new secret realm opening over the Reach, and there is only room at the mouth for one company. {elu_rv} got there a day ahead of you. {elu_rvc} has had a chair put out. {elu_m} has not stopped looking at that chair, and {em_he} asks if you would like it moved, and how far.

choices.text: Move the chair

effects.log: It goes quite a long way. So do several of the people who were sitting near it.

choices.text: Challenge them to go in first, and come out with more

effects.log: Whichever company comes out with the most may keep the mouth. {elu_rvc} laughs, and sets out a second chair.

events.text: The Ministry of Rites has decreed a formal display between {elu_the} and {elu_rv}, before the Court, so that everyone can be reminded of who is in favour. Nobody asked either company. {elu_rvc} sends you a note: they mean to win it, and they would be obliged if nobody were hurt who was going to be needed later.

choices.text: Answer: "Nobody needed later will be"

effects.log: You mean it as a threat. {elu_rvc} frames it. The display is not at all gentle.

choices.text: Answer: "Agreed", and drill them for perfection

effects.log: There is not a mark on anyone by the end, and it is the most frightening thing the Court has seen in an age.

events.text: {elu_rvc} has sent you their blade, in a long box, by barge. It is not a surrender, as the note explains. It is only that they have decided to sit out the next ten thousand years in a very quiet garden, and they thought you should have it, as it would only upset the gardeners. {elu_The} have been told. It is quiet at the mess table.

choices.text: Keep it above the door

effects.log: It makes the door look small. The next person who says you have no rivals gets shown it.

choices.text: Visit the garden

effects.log: You spend a year there, and you lose at a board game many times, on purpose and otherwise.

events.text: The Rolls have been brought up to date, and {elu_rv} stand above {elu_the} on every list that counts, and will go on standing there for as long as anyone can foresee. {elu_rvc} has sent over a jar of something and a polite note that does not refer to any of this. {elu_m} has looked at the jar and wants to know if it is poisoned.

choices.text: Drink it with {elu_m}

effects.log: It is very good. It tastes of a long view. You start making plans of about the right length.

choices.text: Send them back something better

effects.log: It takes you forty years to find it. {elu_rvc}, on opening it, is reported to have laughed.

events.text: You no longer hold the seat that {elu_the} were raised under. The Rolls have noticed: a clerk has come, very politely, to ask under what heading they should now be carried. {elu_m} has poured the clerk a drink and has been listening to all of it, with no change of expression, for about a century so far.

choices.text: Under the seat. They stay

effects.log: They stay on the isle and serve the next hand. The name stays on the Rolls too, with yours beside it, for as long as there are Rolls.

choices.text: Under your name, as a private company

effects.log: It takes some stamps. It also takes a good many of them, and it will take a good many stones to keep them fed.

choices.text: Strike them from the Rolls

effects.log: The clerk blinks. The company disperses over the Isles, and you will meet them, here and there, for the next ten thousand years.

events.text: The Isles have a saying now, about a stubborn thing: "like asking {elu_the} to move." You heard it from a child of three hundred. There is a ledge on the Reach that has their name on it, on the Court's own charts. The Rolls take up a shelf of their own, which is a thing most ministries never live to see.

choices.text: Have someone read you the whole shelf

effects.log: It takes eleven years. There are some things in it you would not have put in.

choices.text: Burn the oldest volume, for the young ones to wonder

effects.log: Now nobody can check the part about the sea. {elu_m} is deeply impressed, and says so.

events.text: There is a very small entry on the Rolls, in a very old hand, that the clerk turned up by accident. It says that from below, from a place nobody here can be bothered to look at, somebody still sends a tribute of rice in the name of {elu_old}. They have been doing it for longer than the record covers. The clerk wants to know whether this is anything to do with you.

choices.text: "Who is it from?"

effects.log: Nobody knows. Up here it is treated as a very tiny mystery. You find that you think about that rice a good deal.

choices.text: "No."

effects.log: The clerk nods, and goes away. There is an odd lump in your throat, and you could not tell anybody what it is.

events.text: You hear from one who came up the white stairs that a company below goes on drilling on a certain hill, under a banner called {elu_old}. They have no idea why that hill. There is a rule that one place at the table is kept empty, and they cannot remember who it is for. You look down over the edge, for longer than you usually do.

choices.text: Send a little rain to that hill

effects.log: It is against several rules. It is not much rain. Nobody ever finds out.

choices.text: Turn away

effects.log: It is a long way down, and you have things to do here. It takes you a while to start doing them.

events.text: Your domain has priests and it has weather, and neither of them is much use in a fight with a god. So you go through the prayers of the last hundred years for those who asked for something unusual, like strength to stand somewhere bad, and you call them up. Some have been dead a while. They stand on your plain, looking confused, and you call them {elu_name}: your part of Heaven's Host.

choices.text: Let them keep their old names

effects.log: They keep them. Worshippers soon begin to pray to them by name, for small things, and this seems to help.

choices.text: Give them each a star

effects.log: A very small one. They are shy of it at first. Your sky looks better, and so does your standing.

events.text: A god with a domain is a god with borders, and the Surveyors are always coming round to measure them. You have decided that the next time they do, someone will walk with them. {elu_name} is what you will call them, those who do the walking. They are lesser gods and old heroes and a very large dog. The dog was not your idea.

choices.text: Keep the dog

effects.log: The dog is the best of them, as it happens. The Surveyors become noticeably more accurate.

choices.text: Give the dog a shrine and a command

effects.log: It accepts, with a certain gravity. It has a small following by spring.

events.text: A General of Heaven commands the Host, in the sense that the Host has heard of you. You would like a few of its people to have actually met you. You pick them out of the Ninth Division, the ones who still salute with the old hand, and you stand them on the Gate's long wall. You tell them they are {elu_name}, and that you are not going to explain it.

choices.text: Have the Court enter it

effects.log: The Heavenly Court has it entered, in a book that is older than death. A Judge asks why. You say it is for the look of the thing.

choices.text: Keep them off the books

effects.log: You will be asked about this one day by someone who can see through the books. You are looking forward to it.

events.text: They have made you a keeper of a gate that nobody has come to in nine thousand years. It is a good post with a very good view. You go around the watchtowers on a slow evening, picking those who still look out at the dark as if something were coming. There are not many of them. {elu_name}, you tell them, and they do not ask you what it means.

choices.text: Tell them what is really out there

effects.log: You tell them. They nod. They had rather thought so, and they go back to their towers.

choices.text: Double the watch on the far gate

effects.log: Nothing comes. It goes on not coming, in a more organized way. They are the first happy people you have seen up here.

events.text: The elder gods of your pantheon have thrones, and each throne has its train: a good many people carrying things. You have asked whether you might not have a few who carry swords. There is a silence that lasts a season. In the end somebody very large and very old says that {elu_name} sounds a pleasant name, and asks you who you intend to use it on.

choices.text: "Whoever is left, when you have finished"

effects.log: A very large laugh rolls across several domains. Crops are affected. You have your company.

choices.text: "Nobody, I hope"

effects.log: That is very well said, they tell you. No one believes it, and it was not intended to be believed, and it is all quite civil.

events.text: You have only been standing with this pantheon for a few thousand years, and they still ask where you are from. You have picked your people from the small ones: gods of bridges and of minor rivers, a god of one particular well. They have never been asked to do anything. They are {elu_name} now, and they stand in a very straight line, trembling, and shining a little.

choices.text: Teach them to fight, yourself

effects.log: It is like teaching a well to fight. It takes a long time. But nobody ever expects it of a well.

choices.text: Teach them to be seen

effects.log: They learn it. A god of a minor river who walks with a straight back is a surprising thing to meet, in the wrong valley.

events.text: The first prayer ever addressed to {elu_the} has come in. It is from a small child on your plain, and it asks them to do something about a neighbour's goose. {elu_m} has brought it to you in both hands. {em_He} is entirely serious, and so, you now understand, are they all, and you have no idea how you are supposed to feel.

choices.text: Deal with the goose

effects.log: Four lesser gods and a very large dog deal with the goose. It is a holy day in that village for the next three hundred years.

choices.text: Send the child a dream, about geese

effects.log: It is a good dream. The child grows up to keep geese, with a certain authority.

events.text: Something has been nibbling at the edge of your domain, a field here, a stream there, and the Surveyor says the maps have started to disagree. {elu_m} has walked the line and come back with odd burrs on {em_his} robe. {elu_The} could march the whole border in glory, shining, for the worshippers to see; or walk it one night at a time, in plain shapes.

choices.text: In glory, with the bells

effects.log: Your worshippers come out on their roofs. So does whatever has been nibbling.

choices.text: One night at a time

effects.log: They go out in plain coats, and they ask the farmers. {elu_m} comes back with a new kind of burr.

events.text: The pilgrims to your great shrine have stopped arriving. It may be the road. It may be that somebody has got hold of the road. {elu_m} would like to know whether {elu_the} are permitted to appear to mortals and ask them what they saw, and whether {em_he} might wear the hat.

choices.text: Appear to all of them, on the road

effects.log: There is going to be a lot of fainting. It should be very clear who owns this road by the end of it.

choices.text: Go as pilgrims, and walk it

effects.log: {elu_m} blisters. It is a new experience. {em_He} reports on it at length.

events.text: A god of another pantheon keeps a shrine in your valley, with a staff of two and a very nice bell. The pantheons have been at peace for an age, and it would be a shame. {elu_m} points out that the bell is in fact stolen, from you, at a date {em_he} can prove.

choices.text: Take the bell, in broad day

effects.log: It is a very loud bell. It rings all the way home. Everyone in Heaven knows by evening.

choices.text: Swap it for a good copy

effects.log: {elu_m} takes a bell-founder from your plain, who is about to have a very strange night.

events.text: A rival's offerings pass across a corner of your plain on their way up, as they have for a thousand years, by a treaty that nobody has read. {elu_m} has read it. There is a word in it that has changed its meaning. By the new meaning, those offerings have been yours for the last four hundred years, and you are owed.

choices.text: Seize the next procession

effects.log: A great many mortals carrying fruit are extremely surprised, and so is the rival.

choices.text: Send a bill

effects.log: {elu_m} writes it out, in the old style, with interest. It is the most hostile thing you have ever signed.

events.text: Everyone in the Pantheon falls silent when you enter, and starts talking again a little too soon after you leave. {elu_m} has taken up a post as cupbearer for one of the elders. {em_He} has been told that nobody ever looks at a cupbearer. You could use what {em_he} hears at once, or wait.

choices.text: Use it now

effects.log: You answer a question in council before it is asked. It is very satisfying. You can feel several heads turn to the cupbearer.

choices.text: Wait, and pour

effects.log: A very long time goes by. {elu_m} now knows a great deal about wine.

events.text: The Book of Fates is not to be read by anyone. There is a clerk who reads it to check the spelling, however, and {elu_m} has noticed that this clerk has a domain's worth of debts. You might learn the date of something. It is the sort of knowledge that costs more than it is worth, and you already know that.

choices.text: Have {em_him} bring the page

effects.log: A page goes missing from the Book of Fates. Nobody has ever thought what would happen if one did.

choices.text: Only ask a single question

effects.log: One date. {elu_m} comes back looking pale, and will not repeat it until you have sat down.

events.text: Thunder has been going back and forth across the middle of the sky for a century. {elu_foe} has moved on your borders in earnest. Your priests are asking what they should tell the people. {elu_m} has the Host's own banner in one hand and the unit's in the other, and would like to know which it is to be today.

choices.text: The unit's, at the head of it all

effects.log: Your own name, in the front of the storm. Worshippers will tell it for an age, and they will not all tell it kindly.

choices.text: The Host's, in the line with everyone

effects.log: You are a good soldier of Heaven. You do your part. It is a part.

choices.text: Neither. They guard the plain

effects.log: A god who keeps the rain falling on time through a war is not a small thing. {elu_m} is not sure of that, but your farmers are.

events.text: A hand of {elu_foe} has taken one of your rivers, and the fish are confused. It is an insult, and it is meant as an invitation. {elu_m} says the whole of the other side is waiting at the bend, in full array, for you to send your best to get it back. {em_He} thinks it might be quite interesting if you did.

choices.text: Send them to the bend

effects.log: It is a very large battle, for a river. It changes course twice. Your people bring back most of it.

choices.text: Let it go, and dam the source

effects.log: It is a long way from glorious. The other side finds itself holding a large dry ditch.

events.text: {elu_m} used to be the god of a small bridge. It was not much of a bridge, and it washed away some time ago. {em_He} still stops at every stream and looks at it, and at how a person might get across. It has been noticed. The other gods of {elu_the} are very kind about this, in a way that makes {em_him} go quiet.

choices.text: Ask {em_him} to bridge the next stream, for the march

effects.log: It is a very good bridge. It takes {em_him} an afternoon. {em_He} does not look at anyone for a while, and the others cross it carefully.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} that {em_he} is more than that now

effects.log: "Yes," {elu_m} says, very politely, looking at the stream.

events.text: There is a village on your plain with a ford that drowns somebody every few years. The people have started to leave out a little rice at the bank. They have no idea for whom. {elu_m} has been going down there in the evenings, and you only found out because the Surveyor wants to know why there is a very small domain on the map that nobody ever claimed.

choices.text: Let {em_him} have it, and call it a posting

effects.log: It is the smallest posting in Heaven. It is worth more to {em_him} than your own plain would be, and {em_he} comes up to the drill each morning with wet feet.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} that it has to stop

effects.log: It stops. The rice is still there the next year. {em_He} walks by that bank, on {em_his} way somewhere else, and does not look.

events.text: There is a great war in Heaven, and the Host needs a crossing over the Silver Stair for the whole of its left wing. It has been asked for and refused by much greater gods than {elu_m}, as they would have to give their whole divinity to it. {em_He} has come to ask for your leave. {em_He} says it is really quite simple. {em_He} has been practising.

choices.text: Give it

effects.log: The left wing crosses. For an age afterwards, the mortal children of that plain, stepping over any stream, will say a certain small word for luck.

choices.text: Refuse, and find another way

effects.log: You find one, at great cost. {elu_m} looks at you for a long time, and then goes back to {em_his} ford, and builds it. It is the best bridge there has ever been, and gods come to look.

events.text: You have received a very respectful complaint from your priests: the people on the east side of the plain have started to pray to {elu_m} and not to you. It is mostly for small things. They say {em_he} answers. {elu_m} is mortified and has come to apologise, standing very straight and glowing more than {em_he} should.

choices.text: Say that it is fine, and take the small prayers off your list

effects.log: You are a great god. There were an awful lot of small prayers. It is actually a relief.

choices.text: Order {em_him} to stop answering

effects.log: {em_He} stops. The people on the east side are quite puzzled, and they go on asking, for a long time.

events.text: There is a shrine now. It is small, and it is on your land, and it has {elu_m}'s face on it, not very well done. A delegation from the Heavenly Court has called to ask whether a lesser god in your service is building a following under your nose, and whether you have considered what happened to the last god who let this happen. They did not stay for tea.

choices.text: Build the shrine a proper roof

effects.log: It is an open answer, and the whole sky can see it. {elu_m} looks at the roof, and then at you, as though you had given {em_him} a sword.

choices.text: Have {elu_m} take it down {em_him}self

effects.log: {em_He} does it. {em_He} takes it down stone by stone, and some people come and watch {em_him} do it. They do not understand who it is they are watching.

events.text: It has come to it. {elu_m} has more worshippers now than some of the Elder Lineages, and a Pantheon has written to offer {em_him} a seat. There is a good case that a domain could be carved out of the east of yours, quite peacefully. {em_He} has come to you first. {em_He} has been standing on your plain since sunrise, and everyone in your Heaven is waiting to see.

choices.text: Carve it out yourself, and give it to {em_him}

effects.log: It is the first domain ever given away in living memory. {elu_m} kneels, and gets up as a neighbour. Nobody can say that you lost anything, and you still feel the draught. {em_He} sends {elu_the} to your wars for the rest of time.

choices.text: Offer {em_him} captaincy, and a place at your right hand

effects.log: {em_He} thinks about it for one long afternoon, and takes it. The east side goes on praying to {em_him}, and {em_he} tells them, every time, whose rain it is.

choices.text: Refuse. The plain is yours

effects.log: {em_He} bows. {em_He} is gone by the evening, and a good many prayers go with {em_him}. Next spring, the Pantheon has a new god with a very familiar way of holding a line.

events.text: The Elder Lineages have a way of doing this. One of them has been to see {elu_m}, in the guise of a beggar at a shrine, and has offered to make {em_him} a full god of something, if {em_he} will only mention, when asked, certain Transgressions {em_he} has seen you commit. {em_He} is not sure that {em_he} saw them. {em_He} is sure that you did them.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to say what {em_he} saw

effects.log: You look at {em_him} when you say it. {em_He} goes before the Court. {em_He} has seen, it turns out, very little.

choices.text: Have {em_him} say yes, and take notes

effects.log: Now you know which Lineage. {elu_m} wears a very small new halo for a while, and does not like how it feels.

events.text: There has been too much whispering in the high halls, and now the gods of {elu_the} have begun to receive gifts: small domains, a little worship, nothing anyone could quite object to. {elu_m} has made a list of who got what. {em_He} is on it. {em_He} has not returned {em_his}, {em_he} says, as it would have told them that {em_he} knows.

choices.text: Thank {em_him}, and let them keep the gifts

effects.log: If they are to be bribed, they may as well be well bribed. They laugh, rather shakily, and you hope that you are right.

choices.text: Send a false order, and see who it reaches

effects.log: You find out. So do they. It is a colder sort of Heaven afterwards.

events.text: When a god dies, the people go on praying for a while, because no one has told them. {elu_m} is dead. On the far side of your plain, there is an old woman who still leaves {em_him} rice at a ford. You could answer her. It would be a very small lie, told by a very great power. {elu_The} have asked what you want done.

choices.text: Answer her, in {em_his} voice

effects.log: She lives a long time, and she never finds out. You answer every year. It is the only thing you do that you have told nobody about.

choices.text: Let the prayers go unanswered, and send a true dream

effects.log: You tell her in a dream, as gently as you can manage. She nods in her sleep. In the morning she leaves the rice out anyway.

events.text: They have brought back {elu_m}'s light, in a jar, which is about what is left of a lesser god. It is not a very bright one. It will last a few hundred years, the Surveyor thinks. {elu_The} would like to know what is the custom, and you have to tell them that nobody has ever thought gods of this size needed one.

choices.text: Set it in your own sky

effects.log: A very small new star, just over the east of the plain. The farmers have already got a name for it. It is a rude one, and affectionate.

choices.text: Pour it into the ford

effects.log: It goes out in the water, with no noise. For a season, the fish there are quite remarkable.

events.text: At the Pantheons' long assembly the place beside yours has been given to {elu_rv}, with {elu_rvc} at their head. {elu_way} It is unlikely to be an accident: nothing here ever is. {elu_rvc} inclines their head by the exact amount the rules allow. {elu_m} inclines {em_his} by a fraction more, and you see the whole row of them notice.

choices.text: Return it, to the hair

effects.log: It is a very correct afternoon. It is written down by four separate recording angels.

choices.text: Ask them about their river

effects.log: It is a very low blow. {elu_rvc} laughs out loud, in Assembly, which has not been done for some time.

events.text: A new-born domain has opened on the border of two pantheons, a raw little plain with no god on it, and it will belong to whoever is standing on it at the first sunrise. {elu_rv} are already marching. {elu_rvc} has sent you the customary notice, and {elu_m} has sent it back with corrections. There is not a lot of night left.

choices.text: Run for it

effects.log: It is a very undignified night for a group of gods. There is a good deal of pushing at the end of it.

choices.text: Get the first farmers there first

effects.log: A plain belongs to whoever it prays to. You land a handful of very confused people, with seed.

events.text: The Heavenly Court has called a Trial of the Hosts. {elu_The} and {elu_rv} are to take the field in front of the Judges, with nobody to die, unless they do. {elu_rvc} has asked if you might both agree on a rule against anything that would darken the sun. {elu_m} wants it noted that this rule is aimed at {em_him}, and {em_he} is flattered.

choices.text: Refuse the rule

effects.log: The sun is, in fact, darkened. The Judges take note of it, in writing, as do your farmers.

choices.text: Accept, and win within it

effects.log: It is the kind of win that only other gods can appreciate. There are quite a few of them, and they do.

events.text: {elu_rvc} has come to your plain alone, walking, as mortals walk. They look at your fields for some time. "Your people are the better," they say at last. "I wanted to see what you feed them." You show them. It is mostly rice. They ask if they might have some seed to take home. {elu_The} watch this from the wall, and do not know where to look.

choices.text: Give it, with instructions

effects.log: It grows very well on their plain, you hear. It is the most comfortable peace you have ever made.

choices.text: Keep them for supper

effects.log: It goes on for about a year. You had not known how lonely it is up here until you found someone to be rude to.

events.text: It is settled: when the pantheons tell stories now, it is {elu_rv} who come over the hill at the end. {elu_The} have a good supporting part. {elu_m} has collected all the versions, and has made a little chart of how often you are mentioned, and how many ways there are of saying "also present".

choices.text: Ask to hear the best version

effects.log: It is quite good. You come out of it rather well, from behind. You have it sung at dinner.

choices.text: Have your priests start a new one

effects.log: It takes a few thousand years to catch on. They have got plenty of those.

events.text: You have lost the seat that {elu_the} were sworn to. They have been asking the Surveyors whether an oath to a god outlasts the god's position. It is a surprisingly open question, it turns out, with a very long literature. {elu_m} has read most of it, and comes to you with {em_his} finger still marking the place.

choices.text: They stay with the domain. Oaths to the place

effects.log: They stay on. The plain goes on being guarded. In the Book of Fates the name stays, and yours beside it.

choices.text: They come with you, if they will

effects.log: Several of them do. A god with no domain and a few devoted followers is an old story, and not one with a happy end.

choices.text: Release them from all of it

effects.log: You say the words. They go out like lamps, one by one, back to their rivers and their bridges. {elu_m} waves.

events.text: A very new god, on being shown round the Pantheons, has asked which of the great powers {elu_the} are. It is explained to them that they are a company. The new god plainly does not believe it, and you get a good account of the conversation from {elu_m}, who was the one showing them around, and who has been dining out on it.

choices.text: Have the new god to dinner

effects.log: They sit at the table very upright, and ask for the story of the river. {elu_m} tells it. It has grown.

choices.text: Tell {elu_m} not to be so pleased about it

effects.log: {em_He} promises. {em_He} goes on being pleased about it, more quietly, for some thousands of years.

events.text: The Book of Fates has a marginal note, which a clerk is very keen to show you, as it appears to have your hand. It is against a company called {elu_old}, long gone, on a world you do not recall. It says only: "I should have gone back for them." The clerk is hoping you might initial it, so the page can be closed.

choices.text: Initial it

effects.log: You do. Your hand knows how. The clerk goes off pleased. You stay where you are for a while, and the rain falls late on your plain.

choices.text: Leave the page open

effects.log: It is very irregular. The clerk is too frightened to say so. It is the one open page in the whole of that volume.

events.text: This world has its halls and its old quarrels, and you have only lately had the means to do what you are doing now. You call a few of your students out behind the woodpile, and you say that if the kingdom's levy ever comes up this road, it had better find someone waiting for it. {elu_name}, you call them. It is a big name for five people and a woodpile.

choices.text: Have them make a banner of their own

effects.log: It is hideous. It is flown from the woodpile, and there is a certain pride taken in that.

choices.text: Drill them till the name fits

effects.log: It takes years, and a lot of wood. You had not known that you could be so patient.

events.text: Everyone knows how the kingdoms take a hall: a levy of farmers, a very polite captain, and then a tax. You have grown tired of waiting for it. You go through your people for those who will stand and not shout, and you tell them what they are now: {elu_name}. Nobody in this world has ever done it this way. You cannot say how you know that it can be done.

choices.text: Send word to the Pillar-Keepers of your world

effects.log: They have no form for it. They write it down, anyway, on the pillar. You have the feeling that something very far off is pleased.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let them find out

effects.log: They do find out, as it happens, one spring. The polite captain goes home with a very different report.

events.text: Your people have a wall and a well and three generations of knowing which neighbours are lying. It has never had anything you could call an army. Your cousins come out into the courtyard with what they have, which is mostly hoes and some very old swords. You look along the row with great seriousness, and you tell them that they are {elu_name}.

choices.text: Show them the proper way to hold a hoe

effects.log: There is, in fact, a proper way. Rumours begin to spread, around the valley, about what your people can do with a hoe.

choices.text: Sell the good ox, and buy them swords

effects.log: The ploughing is a good deal harder that year. Your cousins stand up straighter, though, and they plough in formation.

events.text: There has been a feud with the other end of the valley since before the kingdoms had names. You have just decided that from now on it is going to be conducted properly. The people you choose gather in the kitchen of the oldest cook in the valley, and she goes on cooking, and it is she who actually says the name aloud: "{elu_name}. Well. Sit down and eat something, then."

choices.text: Eat

effects.log: It is a very good soup. It is, in its way, the oath. No one who has had it ever lets the family down.

choices.text: Ask her what she thinks of it

effects.log: She tells you. It takes the rest of the evening, and it covers quite a number of people you thought were dead. You change several of your plans.

events.text: A kingdom's levy is farmers and their sons, called up at harvest and sent home at the first snow. You sit up with the muster lists and pick out those who came back last time without being carried. They can stay on through the winter, you tell them, on real pay, and have a name. {elu_name}. They look at you with great doubt. It is the pay they believe in.

choices.text: Pay them a year in advance

effects.log: The treasury squeaks. They have never been paid in advance by anyone. They do not know how to look at you.

choices.text: Promise them land instead

effects.log: It is a good promise. All of them have heard one like it. You will have to keep this one.

events.text: The lords of the outer valleys bring their own levies to your muster and go home when they feel like it. You have grown tired of counting who has come. In the yard of the old keep, you stand up a few dozen who owe nobody but you, with a name that was not on anyone's banner yesterday. {elu_name}. The lords have already started writing to one another.

choices.text: Invite the lords to come and see them drill

effects.log: They come, all of them, and they stand at the rail, and they go home rather thoughtful.

choices.text: Keep them in the keep, out of sight

effects.log: It will be a matter of some interest, on the day they first come out.

events.text: There is a stone on the old road, carved with a name nobody can read, and travellers have started to say it was put there by whoever made the world. {elu_m} has been sent to clear the bandits away from it. {em_He} has come back and says that {em_he} has got rid of them, and also, that {em_he} would like to ask you something about that stone.

choices.text: Ask {em_him} to leave it where it is

effects.log: {em_He} leaves it. On the way out {em_he} touches it. {elu_The} all start to do so, for luck, and you find that you do it too, and you do not ask yourself why.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} you know nothing about it

effects.log: This is true, as far as you are aware. {em_He} seems to find that disappointing. So, for some reason, do you.

events.text: The harvest carts have to reach the river towns before the rains, and there are people on the road who know it. {elu_m} has been over the ground. {elu_The} can march beside the carts with the banner up, or can go on ahead a day and see who is waiting.

choices.text: Beside the carts, banner up

effects.log: Let them see it and go home. {elu_m} shoulders the ugly banner.

choices.text: Ahead by a day, on foot

effects.log: It is a quiet job. {elu_m} takes the ones who can keep their mouths shut.

events.text: A lord in the next valley has dammed the stream, and your people's fields are dry. Everyone has written letters. {elu_m} has been to look at the dam. {em_He} says it is well made, and that it could stop being a dam in one night, or it could be made to leak slowly, in a way that would bring its builder to ruin.

choices.text: In one night

effects.log: They take a lot of rope, and nobody sleeps. The whole valley will hear it.

choices.text: A slow leak

effects.log: It is a patient sort of revenge. {elu_m} seems to have a talent for it.

events.text: A pedlar has been coming through three times a year, and asks a lot of questions for someone who sells so few needles. {elu_m} has bought a good many needles by now. {em_He} would like to know if you would rather have the pedlar, or whoever it is who is paying for the questions.

choices.text: Take the pedlar, tonight

effects.log: It will be over quickly. {elu_m} has already got the sack.

choices.text: Keep on buying needles

effects.log: You have more needles than you will ever want. {elu_m} goes down the road a mile behind the cart.

events.text: The kingdoms have been at it again, over a river and a marriage, and {elu_foe} has called out the levy on every road. It has come to your door. {elu_m} says the captain outside is very young and very polite. {elu_The} are at the back gate, with their ugly banner, waiting to be told which of three things they are to do.

choices.text: Meet them on the road

effects.log: It is a short, ugly fight, in a turnip field. It will be sung about, for some reason.

choices.text: Hold the gate, and let them starve

effects.log: They are farmers. They want to get home for the harvest as much as anyone. It goes on all autumn.

choices.text: Pay them to go around

effects.log: It costs a good deal. Your people do not like it. They are all still there at the end.

events.text: A war has come through this valley every generation since the kingdoms began. {elu_foe} is the name this time. The old ones are already burying the seed corn. {elu_m} has looked at the road, and at the ford, and at {elu_the}, and at you. "You can have the ford," {em_he} says. "Or you can have them alive in the spring. I do not see how you can have both."

choices.text: The ford

effects.log: They hold it for nine days. It is the longest anybody has ever held anything around here.

choices.text: Alive in the spring

effects.log: It is a bad autumn. It is a better spring than the rest of the valley has.

events.text: {elu_m} has asked you an odd question, at the end of a long march. {em_He} wants to know whether you have ever noticed that the mountains here are very well arranged. That the rivers go where you would want them to go. {em_He} has been thinking about it for years. Nobody else seems to find it strange. {em_He} looks at you as if you might know something.

choices.text: Say that you have noticed

effects.log: {em_He} nods, slowly, and is very quiet for the rest of the march. You did not know that you were going to say it.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to get some sleep

effects.log: {em_He} does. You lie awake yourself a little while, looking at how the mountains are arranged.

events.text: {elu_m} has been going to the Pillar-Keepers and asking them who wrote down the first name. They have told {em_him} to stop. {em_He} has found an old carving, which shows a figure looking down at the world from somewhere else, and there is something about its way of standing. {em_He} has brought you a rubbing of it, and {em_he} holds it up next to you, and looks from one to the other.

choices.text: Burn the rubbing

effects.log: {em_He} watches you do it, without a word. {em_He} has another one, and you both know it. {em_He} has also learned something from your burning it.

choices.text: Ask to keep it

effects.log: It is on your wall for the rest of your life. It really does not look like you. You have looked at it a great many times.

events.text: {elu_m} is old now, and {em_he} has worked it out, or says so. {em_He} sends for you. {em_He} has got a very long list of questions, and it ends with one that {em_he} would like you to carry up, if it should ever happen that you are able to. "Ask them why they made the winters so long," {em_he} says. "That is all. I am not angry. I would simply like to know."

choices.text: Promise to ask

effects.log: {em_He} dies quite satisfied, and you have no idea what you have promised. You do not forget it. You have the feeling that you are not going to forget it for a very long time.

choices.text: Say that it was so the spring would count

effects.log: You do not know why you said that. {elu_m} looks at you, and laughs till {em_he} coughs, and gets better, in a way the physician cannot explain. {em_He} captains the unit for another twenty years.

events.text: The levy always has a drummer, and it is always some thin child. Yours is {elu_m}, who is not a child now, and who still beats the old call on the march, and will not change it. Nobody knows where the call came from. Every kingdom's levy uses it, and it is older than any of them. {em_He} says it is just a very good rhythm for walking.

choices.text: Ask {em_him} to teach it to all of them

effects.log: There is an improvement in the marching. There is a certain hum in the column, too, and you could swear the crows keep time.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to learn the new one

effects.log: {em_He} learns it. {em_He} plays it correctly. Nobody can quite keep in step any more.

events.text: In the last fight, the two lines stopped for a moment. You all saw it. {elu_m} had kept on beating, right through, and the enemy's drummer had picked up the call across the field, and for about ten breaths nobody on either side was able to remember what they were doing. Now there are officers on both sides asking if that person can be got rid of.

choices.text: Keep {em_him}, and put a guard on {em_him}

effects.log: The guard starts to walk in step within the week. The officers go on writing letters.

choices.text: Move {em_him} to the baggage train

effects.log: {em_He} goes. The baggage train develops excellent morale. There are no more of those ten breaths.

events.text: Two kingdoms are drawn up across the barley, and {elu_m} walks out between them with the drum, all alone, as nobody told {em_him} to, and starts up the old call. On the far side somebody takes it up, and then somebody else. {elu_The} are looking at you. It would take only one word from you to have that drum stopped, and you are the only one here with the rank to say it.

choices.text: Let {em_him} play

effects.log: Nobody fights that day. They do not know why. They eat each other's barley-bread and go home. {elu_m} is still walking, when last seen, and the call goes with {em_him}.

choices.text: Have {em_him} brought in, gently

effects.log: They bring {em_him} in. {em_He} comes without any fuss. The battle is fought, and it is won. {em_He} goes on drumming for you, for many years, and it is never quite that call again.

events.text: They have carried {elu_m} home on a door, as is done here. The Pillar-Keepers have sent someone to write the name, and that person has asked you how it is spelled. {elu_The} are standing in the rain with their ugly banner. You spell it out. It looks very small on the stone, for all the people it took to get it there.

choices.text: Have it cut deeper

effects.log: The mason looks at you, and takes out a bigger chisel. It will be readable for a good while yet.

choices.text: Stand in the rain with them

effects.log: Nobody tells you to go in. You all stand there till it is dark, and the door is taken back to where it came from.

events.text: Word has come down the road that {elu_m} will not be coming back along it. Some of {elu_the} had been saving a place by the fire. An old woman of the valley has asked you whether it is true that in the place beyond, whoever made this world looks after those who walked it well. You had thought you had nothing to say on that subject.

choices.text: Say that you are sure of it

effects.log: You sound very sure. You do not know where that comes from. She nods, and goes home, and you stay out in the cold for a little longer.

choices.text: Say that you do not know

effects.log: She nods. She had only wanted to see what you would say. "Nor does anyone," she says, and she pats your hand.

events.text: At the great harvest fair, the people lounging around the wrestling ring are {elu_rv}, known in every valley hereabouts, with {elu_rvc} at their head. {elu_way} {elu_m} has been staring at them for some time. {em_He} would like to know how much you think it would cost to buy {elu_rvc} a drink, and whether it would be more if one poured it on them.

choices.text: Buy the drink

effects.log: They are very good company. You learn a good deal, and so do they.

choices.text: Enter the ring

effects.log: It is a friendly throw. It is meant to be seen. {elu_rvc} gets up laughing, with a very careful look in their eyes.

events.text: The lord who is hiring has room for only one company this year, and both of you know it. {elu_rv} have got here first and have pitched their tents on the good ground. {elu_rvc} sends over a very fair offer: the two captains fight it out in the morning, and the loser goes home. {elu_m} has gone to find {em_his} good boots.

choices.text: Do not wait for morning

effects.log: It is a bad night for tents. By sunrise, the question has largely answered itself.

choices.text: Agree, and shake on it

effects.log: You shake on it. It is a beautiful morning, and a lot of people come out to see it.

events.text: It is over the whole valley now, in song: the better company is yours. {elu_rvc} has taken a farm. You rode out to look at it. It is a good farm. They are quite happy, and they have asked you to stay for the harvest, and they would like it known they can still put you on your back. {elu_The} would like to see this tried.

choices.text: Stay for the harvest

effects.log: You are put on your back only twice. The barley comes in fine.

choices.text: Ride on

effects.log: You wave from the road. It is enough. You have been waving back at that farm in your head for some years, as it turns out.

events.text: They sing about {elu_rv} in every valley, and the song has one short verse with your people in it, where they lose. It is a very good verse. {elu_m} has been heard singing it. You take it up with {em_him}. {em_He} says that it is at least the only song with you in it, and that a person takes what they are given.

choices.text: Learn the verse

effects.log: You sing it at the next fair, badly, on purpose. Some people stop thinking it is a joke at your expense. Some do not.

choices.text: Have them drill till the song is wrong

effects.log: It may take years. You have them. {elu_m} grumbles, and is first on the field.

events.text: You have given up, or lost, the seat that {elu_the} were called up under. The steward has read out what is on the list, and it includes "one company, ugly banner." {elu_m} has been sitting on the wall kicking {em_his} heels through all of this. {em_He} wants to know whether {em_he} is on the list too, or whether that is only the banner.

choices.text: Leave them with the seat

effects.log: They will do. The new hand has good sense, and pays. The banner stays up, and they tell it around the valley that you made it.

choices.text: Take them along

effects.log: You now have a good many mouths on the road. {elu_m} jumps down from the wall, and brings the banner, and that seems to be that.

choices.text: Send them home to their farms

effects.log: It is high time, some would say. They go off, in ones and twos. The hoes are still good. The banner goes into somebody's kitchen, and is used for something.

events.text: The Pillar-Keepers of your world have asked for a true account of {elu_the}, to be written up alongside the kingdoms. You have been told it is a great honour. Nobody knows who reads the pillars, and they have a way of lasting. {elu_m} has a good many suggestions as to what should be left out, most of them concerning {em_him}.

choices.text: Leave it all in

effects.log: It takes up a surprising amount of pillar. You have an odd sensation, as it is cut, of someone reading over your shoulder.

choices.text: Keep it short

effects.log: One line, the name and the number of years. It looks very well. It is the first thing anybody notices.

events.text: Up here a betrayal takes its time. You find it in the Rolls: an entry in a clerk's very straight hand, moving {elu_m} from the strength of {elu_the} to the strength of someone else, with effect from nine years ago. {em_He} has gone on drilling with you every morning since. {em_He} is at the rail now, watching you read, and {em_he} does not look away.

choices.text: Send your people after {em_him}, across the Reach

effects.log: It is a long chase, by anyone's standards. They bring back a sleeve. {elu_m} is on the far side of the sky, and everything {em_he} knows went too.

choices.text: Close the Rolls, and let {em_him} go

effects.log: You turn the page. {em_He} bows, at exactly the right depth, and steps off the terrace. You change every signal you own.

choices.text: Ask {em_him} what it would take to come back

effects.log: A long silence. "Nobody has ever asked," {elu_m} says. You will know in a century or so whether that was an answer.

events.text: It has gone round the high halls before it reaches you: {elu_m} has taken a seat at another's table, along with a small star that used to be on your side of the sky. {elu_The} are looking up. A priest on your plain has already asked what the new gap in the constellation means, and how it should be explained to the farmers.

choices.text: Put a price on {em_him}, before the Court

effects.log: It is entered, and it is enormous. {elu_m} sends back a very small offering, by way of receipt.

choices.text: Tell the farmers it was always meant to go

effects.log: They accept that. They are used to you. Nobody on your own side of the sky believes a word.

events.text: {elu_m} has gone over to the other end of the valley, and has taken the ugly banner's second-best drum, and everything {em_he} knows about your wall. {elu_The} have gathered in the yard. Everyone has somebody who saw it coming, now. Somebody has already been sick behind the woodpile, out of pure rage.

choices.text: Go after {em_him} before the snow

effects.log: They catch up at the ford. There is a good deal of shouting, and a cut hand, and {elu_m} gets across. You will not get the drum back.

choices.text: Let {em_him} go, and move the stores

effects.log: It takes a week of hard carrying. You say nothing, and you make sure you are the first to lift.

events.text: A sail you know has come round the end of the chain. It has been three hundred years. {elu_m} stands at its rail, a good deal less splendid than when you saw {em_him} last. {em_He} has come, {em_he} says, across all that air, to tell you that you were right about one thing and to ask if you recall which.

choices.text: Meet {em_him} on the open cloud, and end it

effects.log: It is quite brief, for something that took three centuries. The wind has had what is left by evening.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} you never recalled, and offer the old berth

effects.log: "You are the same fool," {elu_m} says, and throws you a rope. There is a very stiff supper.

choices.text: Send {em_him} away with a jar of the good stuff

effects.log: {em_He} goes off, with the jar. You hear nothing again, except, one day, that the sail was found empty, and very tidy.

events.text: There is someone at the back of the harvest fair with a very old drum, and a limp you gave them. {elu_m} has grown grey. {em_He} comes through the crowd slowly, with people moving aside for no reason they could tell you. "I have a farm now," {em_he} says. "I came to see whether you had one. It would be a pity if only one of us got out."

choices.text: Finish it, behind the wrestling ring

effects.log: It does not take long. You are both old. You pay for the burying, and nobody at the fair knows any of this.

choices.text: Ask whether {em_he} wants {em_his} place back

effects.log: "For what?" {elu_m} says. Then, after a while: "Who is doing the drum, these days?" There is nobody. There is now.

choices.text: Buy {em_him} a drink, and let it lie

effects.log: It is a poor drink. You both finish it. You never see {em_him} again, and in the spring a neighbour tells you about the farm.

events.text: With {elu_m} gone, the isle has nobody to read out the orders, and {elu_the} go on doing what they were last told, which up here could go on for a very long time. A junior of only two hundred has been standing at the rail for a week, reading the old orders aloud in a shaking voice, because someone should.
