choices.text: Give that one the token

effects.log: The elder immortals look at you with a certain pity. In a century, they are taking orders from that voice, and it no longer shakes.

choices.text: Give it to the most senior

effects.log: It is correct, and it will be in the Rolls by morning. Nobody could say a thing against it, and nobody does.

events.text: Someone must walk at the head of {elu_the} now that {elu_m} is gone. In this realm it is decided by whose light is brightest, as a rule, and that has been a very poor rule for some time. They have lined up on the plain at dawn. They are all trying, very hard, not to shine at you.

choices.text: Choose the dimmest

effects.log: A god of one well steps forward, trembling. It has seen a great many things go wrong, from down there, and it does very well.

choices.text: Choose the brightest

effects.log: It is what they expect. It does make a very fine sight from the farms.

events.text: Nobody has picked up the stick that {elu_m} carried. It is leaning by the door, where it was left. {elu_The} go around it. An old neighbour tells you that a thing like that does not pick itself up, and that you have been standing there rather a long time looking at it.

choices.text: Hand it to the one who sweeps the yard

effects.log: There is some surprise. The one who sweeps has been watching all this for years, as it turns out.

choices.text: Hand it to the strongest

effects.log: It is a short, sensible conversation. By supper, nobody goes around the door any more.

events.text: The isle has passed to you, and with it {elu_the}: immortals who were serving under this roof long before you came. {elu_m} has come to the terrace with the token held out in one hand, not quite offering it. "We have done this before," {em_he} says. "We would like to know if you are going to be the sort who needs it explained."

choices.text: Ask {em_him} to explain it

effects.log: {em_He} considers this for some time. "That," {em_he} says, "is the right sort." It takes about nine years.

choices.text: Take the token, and give your first order

effects.log: It is a good order. They carry it out at once. It will be a hundred years before you find out what they really thought.

events.text: You have the walled yard now, and the debts, and {elu_the}, who taught you to climb that wall when you were small and who have now started calling you by a title. {elu_m} does it very stiffly. There is a place at the table that nobody will take. Everybody has gone quiet, to see whether it is going to be you.

choices.text: Sit in your own old place

effects.log: You sit where you always sat, down at the end. It takes them a moment. Somebody laughs, and then passes you the salt.

choices.text: Take the seat at the head

effects.log: You sit. It is a very hard chair. {elu_m} nods, once. It is going to be all right, or it is going to be something.

events.text: You stop by the barracks on the windward side, and you find that nobody there ever met anyone you knew. It has been nine hundred years. They have a small shrine to a former captain of {elu_the}, whom you remember chiefly for snoring. A very earnest young immortal explains to you the deeper meaning of it, at some length.

choices.text: Tell them about the snoring

effects.log: There is a horrified silence, and then the most enormous laughter you have heard on this isle in an age.

choices.text: Let them have their shrine

effects.log: You leave a small offering. Then, in a moment when nobody is looking, you bow to it, for the snoring.

events.text: A clerk from the Rolls has come to ask if {elu_the} are one company or several, since nobody on the present strength has ever met the people who first held the name, and no part of the original banner survives but a stain. It is a real legal question. {elu_m} is rather enjoying it. There is a form.

choices.text: Sign that they are the same company

effects.log: You sign. You look out at them for a while, those strangers with the old name. You had not known you would mind.

choices.text: Sign that they are not: let them be new

effects.log: The clerk takes it away. A new line in the Rolls, the old one ruled off. {elu_The} throw a very long party.

events.text: A very young star has been sent to you with the new draft for {elu_the}, and has been told to say a prayer as it arrives. It has been taught that you were at the making of the plain. You were not. It seems to have been a long time since anyone here could tell the difference. {elu_m} waits to see what you will say.

choices.text: Tell it the truth

effects.log: It is rather crushed. It is also, you notice, the first of them who ever argues with you, and you keep it near.

choices.text: Accept the prayer

effects.log: You accept it. It is well-meant, and you find that it is not as heavy as you had thought it was going to be.

events.text: The mortals on your plain have got a saying that when the old company walks the border, the rain comes on time. The old company is nothing of the sort: there have been eleven, one after another, and it has mostly been the farmers. But the Surveyor has written the saying into the charter. {elu_The} are now, by law, weather.

choices.text: Have them learn something about rain

effects.log: It takes a long time, and they are very bad at it. Your crops improve for reasons nobody could prove.

choices.text: Leave it be

effects.log: Nothing is lost. A god of a minor river is seen looking up at the sky, in a professional way.

events.text: A child of the valley has run up to you to say that a grandparent of theirs was in {elu_the}. So was a grandparent of the child behind them. You look around at the people in this yard, and they all have the same way of standing, and you taught it to someone once. You cannot quite remember who. You think that you had meant to write it down.

choices.text: Have someone write it down

effects.log: They bring out the oldest of them, who has most of it. It goes on the pillar.

choices.text: Show the child the proper way to stand

effects.log: It takes about a minute. The child goes off, very upright, to frighten a goose.

events.text: They have rebuilt the wall. It is a much better wall, and nobody now in {elu_the} remembers the old one, or why it had that gap by the gate, where you all used to go out to look at the weather. There is a very respectful suggestion that you might like to lay the last stone. It would go, exactly, in that gap.

choices.text: Lay it

effects.log: It fits. Everyone cheers. It is a good wall, and you go in by the gate from now on.

choices.text: Have them leave the gap

effects.log: They do not understand. They do it anyway. It becomes a custom, and the young ones go out there to look at the weather.

events.text: You have put {elu_m} into {elu_the}, and everyone in the hall knows how quickly {em_he} got the rank that you gave {em_him}. Nobody has said so. There is a very old farmer among them who has only looked {em_him} up and down, slowly, the way one looks at a calf somebody has paid too much for.

choices.text: Have {em_him} work the same field as the old farmer

effects.log: It is a long, hot season. By the end they are both complaining about you, together, which is a start.

choices.text: Tell the old farmer to mind that field

effects.log: It is your right. The old farmer has been told worse by better. {elu_m} now has one person who will never forgive {em_him}.

events.text: {elu_The} have not had their wages for some time. They have been very good about it. They have started to take their pay in turnips, from people who are glad to have them about, and there is talk in the valley about whose company it is, the one that eats at everybody's table. {elu_m} would like a word.

choices.text: Sell the good ox, and pay them

effects.log: It is a very good ox. The talk stops. The ploughing does not get any easier.

choices.text: Ask the valley to help keep them

effects.log: They agree, at a price: from now on they get a say. It is the sort of thing that goes on growing.

events.text: You gave up the seat, and you did not give up the house, and everyone who matters knows the difference. Nobody has seen you in the hall for a year. So nobody sees a handful of people called out to a tea-house by the back canal, one at a time. They have no banner. They have a name, for use among themselves: {elu_name}.

choices.text: Pay them through the tea-house

effects.log: The tea is very expensive, and the accounts are perfect. The one in the seat will wonder for years why nothing ever quite goes wrong for you.

choices.text: Let the one in the seat find out

effects.log: You leave one small thread showing. A curtain only works if people know there is something behind it.

events.text: The one who sits in your old chair signs what you send, and thanks you for it, and has begun to have ideas. It seems wise to keep a few people who were never on the rolls of that hall. You meet them in the garden, and you go on pruning the whole time. "{elu_name}," you say to a rose, and they understand they have been told.

choices.text: Finish the rose, then give the first order

effects.log: It is a small order. It is carried out by morning, and nobody in the hall can say by whom.

choices.text: Tell them who they are really there to watch

effects.log: They look at the windows of the hall. Nobody says anything. You go on with the rose.

events.text: An auditor from the Ministry of War has come to your camp with two clerks and a very clean coat. The fodder accounts for your banner show a great many horses eating well, and {elu_the} draw rations under no heading the Ministry can find. {elu_m} has offered to show the auditor round the horse lines, in a tone you recognise.

choices.text: Open the real books, and pay what is owed

effects.log: It costs you. The auditor is so startled that the report comes out almost warm. Your household now has a heading, and a line on it.

choices.text: Show the auditor the good horses, twice

effects.log: It is an old trick, and the auditor is too polite to count the same scar twice. It will go in a file somewhere.

events.text: The Ministry has sent down a new regulation: a commander's household guard shall be no more than the following number, drawn from the following regiments, and inspected every spring. It was plainly written with one General in mind. {elu_m} reads it out in the mess tent, in the voice of a very stupid clerk, to great applause.

choices.text: Comply, on paper, down to the last button

effects.log: The spring inspector finds everything correct. It takes a whole company to keep it looking that way.

choices.text: Send the regulation back with your compliments

effects.log: You note that the frontier has not had time to read it. There are those at court who enjoy that a good deal, and those who write it down.

events.text: The Minister of Rites has a nephew. He is twenty, he has very fine boots, and he has been told that service with {elu_the} would look well in a family history. The letter is charming. {elu_m} has been to look at the nephew, and reports in one word that you should not repeat at court. The Minister votes on your budget.

choices.text: Take him, and make him carry water

effects.log: He carries water for two years. To everyone's alarm, he turns out to be rather good. The Minister thinks you are a person of sense.

choices.text: Refuse, with every courtesy

effects.log: The courtesy is noted. So is the refusal. The grain convoys start to arrive late for no reason anyone can name.

events.text: Two of the sergeants in {elu_the} have put in for a commission. They have earned it, and it would take them out of your household and put them over somebody's cousin. Your staff tell you it is impossible. {elu_m} tells you nothing, and leaves their service record on your table, open at the page with the bridge.

choices.text: Fight it through the Ministry

effects.log: It takes a year and several favours you were saving. There are two new officers in the army who were never anyone's cousin.

choices.text: Keep them. You need them here

effects.log: They say they understand. They do. They go on being the best you have, and you can see that it costs them.

events.text: On the eve of the crossing the staff bring you three plans, and all three need someone to hold the far bank alone until the bridge is up. Nobody says who. {elu_m} is standing by the tent flap with {em_his} helmet on already, looking at nothing, with the air of one who has heard this speech before and knows how it ends.

choices.text: Send {elu_the} over first

effects.log: They go across in the dark without a sound. You stand on the near bank until the sun is up, and you count the ones you can see.

choices.text: Send a line regiment, and keep them at your stirrup

effects.log: It is a perfectly sound decision. The regiment holds for most of the morning. {elu_m} takes off the helmet and says nothing at all.

events.text: You have kept {elu_the} at your stirrup through three campaigns, and now the men have a song about it. Not a kind one. It says what they will do when the General's pets are finally sent where the arrows are. It is a good tune. You hear it from the ranks while you are shaving, and {elu_m} has stopped humming.

choices.text: Put your household in the line, in front of them

effects.log: Nobody sings it the next week. There is a new verse by the end of the month, and it is about the left flank, and rather proud.

choices.text: Have the singers flogged

effects.log: It stops at once. Nobody sings anything for quite a long time, and you can hear the whole army not singing.

events.text: The pact says that a cultivator serves the army only with their power hidden, and a Censor has come to your camp with a question about a thing a sentry saw. {elu_m} has been keeping the sentry company. "It was the moon," {em_he} tells you. "On a very wet rock. Everyone agrees. The Censor is going to hear it from all of us, in the same words."

choices.text: Let them lie for you

effects.log: They do it very well. The Censor leaves with a full notebook and a bad cold. You owe them something you cannot pay in silver.

choices.text: Tell them not to, and face it yourself

effects.log: You will not have them perjured. {elu_m} looks at you for some time. The Censor is rather disappointed by how little there is to catch, this time.

events.text: Someone at court has written that a General with a private company, a loyal army and a reputation is a thing the histories have a word for. The memorial is very well argued. The Emperor has read it, you are told, and has not said anything, which is the part that keeps your staff awake. {elu_m} would like to know where you want {elu_the} to sleep.

choices.text: Send them to the capital, under the Throne's own eye

effects.log: You hand your best people to the people who wrote it. They march in, very correct. It is the loudest thing you could have said.

choices.text: Keep them close, and go on as you were

effects.log: Nothing happens. Nothing goes on happening. You begin to sleep in your boots.

events.text: A summons, under the Grand Marshal's seal: a command is falling vacant, far above anything you have held, and they have asked for you. There is one line about your household. It will be absorbed into the Marshal's Guard, with honours, and {elu_the} will cease to appear in the rolls under that name. {elu_m} has already read it. Everyone has.

choices.text: Accept the command, and refuse that line

effects.log: You send it back with the line struck through in your own hand. They give way, in the end, and you have made one very patient enemy in the Ministry.

choices.text: Decline the command

effects.log: You stay where you are, with your people, on the far edge of the map. It is written up as modesty. They know what it was.

events.text: You are growing old for this. {elu_m} has grown older. There is a farm in the Western Hunting Park that nobody has claimed, and a suggestion from the Ministry that a veteran company might be settled on it, in the old way, with a small grant, as a reserve. The papers need your seal. {elu_The} have not said a word about it, and they have all come to look at the soil.

choices.text: Seal it, for the ones who want it

effects.log: Some go. Their children will carry spears for your banner, and they will hoe in step. The rest stay with you for the time you have.

choices.text: Tie the grant to your banner for good

effects.log: It is rather sharp practice. There is now a village that owes its land to your name, and the court has noticed that too.

events.text: They have taken your command away. You are not a General now, and a household guard is not a thing your new rank may keep. Nobody has come to collect {elu_the}, because nobody wants to be the one sent. {elu_m} has pitched the tents in the usual order, a little behind your own, in the part of the camp meant for baggage.

choices.text: Tell them it changes nothing

effects.log: They go on drilling in the baggage lines. The regiment you now serve under finds this extremely funny for about a week, and after that it stops.

choices.text: Tell them they are free to go

effects.log: {elu_m} looks round at the baggage. "Go where?" {em_he} says, and goes back to the tent pegs.

events.text: The order that broke you was read out before the whole army. You stood through it. Afterwards, the sergeants of {elu_the} came to your new tent, which is a good deal smaller, and they have brought the same chair. They set it down in the same place relative to the door. Nobody has mentioned anything. {elu_m} is asking whether you would like your tea.

choices.text: Say yes

effects.log: It is the same bad tea. You will get the command back or you will not. It is remarkable how much less that matters, this morning.

choices.text: Tell them to take the chair away

effects.log: They take it away. You find it outside the tent next morning, with someone sitting in it, on guard.

events.text: You hand in your tally of command, or it is taken from you. It comes to the same. The Ministry's clerk reads from a list: "one household company, so-called," to be returned to the regiments it was drawn from. {elu_m} is standing at attention behind you, with {em_his} boots polished, and the whole of {elu_the} behind {em_him}.

choices.text: Let them go back to the regiments

effects.log: They go, under the name of nobody. Within a year every regiment on the frontier has a sergeant who will not take any nonsense. The chronicle keeps the name.

choices.text: Take whoever will come, as your own

effects.log: A dismissed General with a private company is a thing the Ministry has a form for, and you will hear about it. A few of them are in plain coats at your gate by nightfall.

choices.text: Stand them down yourself, on the parade ground

effects.log: You do it properly, with the drums, before the clerk has finished. Then you walk off the ground by yourself. It is the last order you give.

events.text: The Censor has finished, and the pact has been read, and you are out of the army with your name in a report. {elu_The} have been told they had no idea what you were. They knew perfectly well. {elu_m} has said so, to the Censor, at length, and has been asked to reconsider. {em_He} would like to know what you would have {em_him} do.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to reconsider, and stay in

effects.log: It goes against everything. They stay in. They will get a very poor posting, and the name will go with them, and they will make it mean something there.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to pack

effects.log: {em_He} is packed. So are several others. You had not thought they would be so quick, and then you recall who trained them.

choices.text: Tell them it is finished

effects.log: They hear you out. They break the banner themselves, and you are not asked to watch. You do.

events.text: You chose to go. You have a good reason, and it has nothing to do with them, and that is rather the difficulty. The Army does not let a private company walk out with a retiring commander, but it has been known not to look. {elu_m} has been looking in the other direction for some time, and is waiting to see how far you would like it to go.

choices.text: Leave them to the army

effects.log: You go by yourself, on a very ordinary horse. You find out years afterwards that they have been saluting that horse's stable.

choices.text: Do not look, and do not ask

effects.log: There are rather more people on the road home than you had set out with. None of them will say why they happen to be going that way.

events.text: A hundred years of {elu_the}, by the Rolls. It means nothing up here; a hundred years is a long lunch. But {elu_m} has had a small cake made. There is nobody present who thinks this is sensible, and all of them have come. There is a question of who was there at the start, and it turns out that the answer is you.

choices.text: Cut the cake

effects.log: It is a very small cake. It goes round a very long table, and there is a crumb for each.

choices.text: Tell them about the first banner

effects.log: It was hideous. You had forgotten that it was hideous. They do not believe you, and they want to hear it again.

events.text: A century of {elu_the}. Your priests want a festival, and so does the Surveyor, for reasons of tax. The mortals on your plain have already held four generations of it without being asked. {elu_m} has been to see one, in a plain shape. {em_He} reports that they have got the dance wrong and that it is much better.

choices.text: Go down and see it

effects.log: You stand at the back, in a plain shape. Somebody hands you a rice cake, and tells you that you are doing it wrong.

choices.text: Bless the wrong version

effects.log: A god has now ruled on the matter. Three villages go to law over it for the next thousand years.

events.text: Three hundred years, and not one of the first roster is left. {elu_The} have got an old hall of records now, with a very old immortal in charge who has never held a sword. The old one has come to you with a problem: there are two accounts of the fight at the Sundered Reach, both in your hand, and they do not agree. Which one is to be kept?

choices.text: Keep the worse one

effects.log: The old one blinks. "It is the true one, then," the old one says, and goes off, satisfied. You had not said so.

choices.text: Keep them both

effects.log: It is against all practice. Three hundred years from now, some young scholar is going to have a wonderful time.

events.text: Three hundred years, and a junior of {elu_the} has asked you, with great respect, if it is true that gods were once afraid of you. You have to think about that. You look along the line: a star, a river, the third dog. You cannot actually recall a time when you were not somebody's old story.

choices.text: Say that they still are

effects.log: It gets a very good laugh. It is not quite a joke. You see {elu_m} make a note of it.

choices.text: Say you were the one afraid

effects.log: The junior does not know what to do with that. It is passed from star to star for some time, and it does you more good than the laugh.

events.text: A thousand years. Empires of the world below have gone in that time, and been told of, and nobody here looked up. {elu_m} comes to you with the token worn perfectly smooth, and it is {em_his} own idea to ask: should it be recut? There is nobody left who could tell you what the mark on it once was.

choices.text: Recut it from memory

effects.log: You do it yourself, in a single evening, and it is not the same mark. By the next morning, it is the only one that ever was.

choices.text: Leave it smooth

effects.log: They carry a blank piece of jade now, and they will fight anybody who asks what it means.

events.text: A thousand years of {elu_the}. The Book of Fates has opened a separate volume, on the grounds that the old one would no longer close. A clerk has brought it for your inspection. It starts in the middle of a sentence. {elu_m} is reading over your shoulder, and has put a finger on an entry, and is looking at you. You have no memory of what it says you did.

choices.text: Ask {elu_m} what happened

effects.log: {em_He} tells you. It takes a while. It is not at all flattering, and you have the odd feeling of being introduced to someone.

choices.text: Close it

effects.log: It does not close easily. The clerk has to lean on it. You will have to take what you did on trust, like everyone else.

events.text: Three thousand years. The name of {elu_the} has outlasted two languages. The young immortals pronounce it in a way that makes you wince, and they have a very learned account of what it meant, involving a mountain. {elu_m} has heard it too. It turns out that nobody now alive but you knows that somebody just liked the sound.

choices.text: Tell them the truth of it

effects.log: They listen with perfect courtesy. It is written up as one of your parables. It is taught.

choices.text: Learn the new way to say it

effects.log: It takes you a month. You get it wrong for the rest of your life, and the young ones are too kind to mention it.

events.text: Three thousand years. A very small new god has been assigned to {elu_the}, as a clerk, and has found that all the company's old enemies are gone: dead, or merged, or now on the same side, or worshipped by the same farmers. It has prepared a report suggesting that the unit has no further purpose. {elu_m} has brought it to you, with great enjoyment.

choices.text: Sign it, and go on exactly as before

effects.log: It is filed. The company has now officially had no purpose for some time, and morale has never been higher.

choices.text: Make the small god a captain of something

effects.log: It is terrified, and thorough. Within a century you have several new enemies, carefully documented.

events.text: Ten thousand years. You stand on the terrace of an isle that has moved four times, looking at people who bow to you the way one bows to a mountain. {elu_m} is the seventeenth to hold that token. Somebody has left a bad rice cake on your step, as is apparently done. You have to go back quite a long way to remember why that makes your throat close.

choices.text: Eat it

effects.log: It is a very bad rice cake, and exactly right. You do not tell them. You have the next one left out on purpose.

choices.text: Go down and join the drill

effects.log: There is a moment of pure terror along the line. Then it passes, and they find that you are a little slow on the turn, and they are very gentle about it.

events.text: Ten thousand years. Your plain has been a sea, and it has been a sea again. {elu_The} have outlived the river that one of them was the god of. {elu_m} asks if you ever think about stopping. It is not a challenge. It seems to be something {em_he} has been meaning to ask for a while, on a slow evening, the two of you on the wall.

choices.text: Say that you do

effects.log: {em_He} nods. Neither of you adds anything, and it goes on being a good evening. It is the most you have said to anybody in an age.

choices.text: Say that you would like to see how it comes out

effects.log: {elu_m} laughs. "So would I," {em_he} says, and goes off to see about the watch.

events.text: Thirty thousand years. There is an entire minor sect of the Isles now that does nothing but study {elu_the}. They would be very grateful, they say, if you would come and give a talk. You go. A young scholar corrects you on a point of your own life, with footnotes, and is right. Afterwards {elu_m} asks if you enjoyed yourself, and you find, to your surprise, that you did.

choices.text: Ask the scholar to join

effects.log: The scholar is appalled, and comes. It is the first new idea the company has had in about nine thousand years.

choices.text: Send them the true account of the bridge

effects.log: It causes a schism. Two very bitter journals are founded. You read both with pleasure.

events.text: Thirty thousand years. The mortals have stopped telling stories about {elu_the} and have begun simply to assume them, as one does with weather and tax. A god of the younger sort has asked whether the company is an institution or a person. {elu_m} says that {em_he} has never been able to tell, and it has not come up. You are invited to rule on it.

choices.text: Rule that it is a person

effects.log: It takes offence at once at several things. It has a birthday now. The young god regrets having asked.

choices.text: Rule that it is both, and go to lunch

effects.log: This is the correct answer, according to all later commentary. The lunch is described in some detail.

events.text: A hundred years of {elu_the}, more or less; nobody around here counts as well as they used to. The ugly banner has been re-sewn so many times that there is not a thread left of the first one. The children of the valley have started a game about it, with sticks. {elu_m} has been made to be the enemy, and is taking it very seriously.

choices.text: Join in

effects.log: You are a very bad enemy, and you are defeated in short order, by someone of six. It is all over the valley.

choices.text: Show them how the left flank really went

effects.log: They listen with shining eyes and go straight back to doing it wrong. It was a much better fight their way.

events.text: The Pillar-Keepers have written to say that a company which has lasted three hundred years must be entered among the kingdoms, for the purposes of their records, and may wish to send an envoy. {elu_m} would like to go. {em_He} has bought a hat. Nobody has ever been an envoy from a woodpile, and you find that you are quite curious how it goes.

choices.text: Send {em_him}, with the banner

effects.log: The kingdoms receive {em_him} with the utmost seriousness, and an awful lot of soup. There is now a small treaty.

choices.text: Decline, with thanks

effects.log: It is enough to be asked. You keep the letter. It goes up in the kitchen, beside the rest.

events.text: It is an age of open sails. The Reach has calmed, for reasons no one can explain, and every chain is trading with every other. The Heavens are full of barges and of very cheerful people with something to sell. {elu_The} have started being asked to escort things. {elu_m} comes back from a run with a new coat, and an expression you have not seen for a long time.

choices.text: Take every contract going

effects.log: It is a good age to be useful in. They have never been so rich, or so bored.

choices.text: Keep them hard, and let the others grow fat

effects.log: They drill on an empty terrace while the barges go by. Nobody remembers quite why, until the next age comes.

events.text: Now the barges have come back to the Reach, a new age of them, after so long, and the young ones of {elu_the} talk of nothing else. You have seen this before. {elu_m} has not, and is very excited. There is a song going around, which you remember in another key. Somebody has already started selling those same hats.

choices.text: Buy a hat

effects.log: It looks ridiculous. It looked ridiculous the last time, too. You are the only one on the isle who knows how long it lasts.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} how this ends

effects.log: {em_He} is very polite about it. {em_He} goes on being excited. You had rather hoped {em_he} would.

events.text: A long quiet has come over the Isles. The factions have stopped speaking to one another, the Calendar gatherings are half empty, and a great many old immortals have closed their doors for a thousand-year sit. {elu_The} have nothing whatever to do. {elu_m} has started a small garden on the windward side, and it is going badly, and {em_he} is very happy.

choices.text: Let them rest

effects.log: They rest. It is the first time in anyone's memory. Some of them turn out to be interesting.

choices.text: Find them someone to study

effects.log: A quiet age is when you learn where everybody has hidden things. {elu_m} sighs, and leaves the garden in good order.

events.text: The quiet has come again. The doors are shut along the chain. {elu_m} has gone back to the windward side, to a garden that was planted by someone whose name you have mislaid, and it has come back rather well. You find yourself walking out there most evenings. It is not as if there is anything to report.

choices.text: Take a hoe

effects.log: You are very bad at it. {elu_m} is courteous. The beans have their own opinion.

choices.text: Sit on the wall

effects.log: You sit on the wall. It is a very good wall for it. In this realm you may not get another age like this one.

events.text: The Reach is burning. No one is quite sure who started it. It is an age of war in the Heavens, as there has been before and will be again, with the sails out, and the Jade Court issuing very stern notes. {elu_m} has already had the company's hair cut. {elu_The} look ten thousand years younger, and they are grinning.

choices.text: Take them to where it is worst

effects.log: You had forgotten how good they are. You had forgotten what it costs, too, and you will be reminded.

choices.text: Hold the isle, and take in whoever comes

effects.log: They come by the thousand. For a generation or so your terraces are full of strangers, and you are a good deal better loved than you were.

events.text: The sails are out again. You knew it before the Court did: your knee told you, or whatever it is that an immortal has in place of a knee. {elu_m} is new to this and very eager. You go down the line of {elu_the}, the ones who have never seen it, and you look at each of their faces in turn, and you try to remember which of them you are going to have to remember.

choices.text: Tell them it will be glorious

effects.log: They believe you. It is what they need. It is even true, in part.

choices.text: Tell them what you told the last lot

effects.log: You give the same speech. It is a very short speech, and you know now which words they will keep.

events.text: It is a fallow age. The cloud is thin and the qi comes slowly. Whole isles have sunk a little, and nobody has the strength to spare for anything so vigorous as a war. {elu_m} reports that half of {elu_the} are asleep at their posts, and that it may be the most sensible thing they could do. The stones are running short.

choices.text: Share out what you have

effects.log: It does not go far. You go without, as long as they can see it. Nobody forgets that for about four thousand years.

choices.text: Send them out to dig for it

effects.log: They go down to the undersides of the isles. They come back very thin, with strange things, and not all of them.

events.text: The cloud has gone thin again. You remember this. You know how long it lasts, more or less, and you know that it does end, and you are the only one of {elu_the} who does. {elu_m} comes to you, grey in the face, wanting to know whether this is the end of everything. You have got the voice for it by now.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} how long

effects.log: You tell {em_him} the number. {em_He} sits down rather suddenly. Then {em_he} gets up, and starts to ration.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} to go and get some sleep

effects.log: You sound exactly like someone you once knew. You stay up in {em_his} place, on the wall, for some time.

events.text: It is a Bright Age. The farmers on your plain have three harvests a year and have forgotten what you are for. The temples are full of cheerful people asking for very small things. {elu_The} have nothing to do but march in the festivals. {elu_m} has been garlanded eleven times this month and is showing signs of strain.

choices.text: Let them enjoy it

effects.log: They do. There is a very stout lesser god by the end of it. You had almost forgotten that it could be like this.

choices.text: Take them out past the border, to keep their edge

effects.log: The farmers wave them off. They come back a century later, lean, and no one has noticed they were gone.

events.text: The Bright Age has come round again, and the young gods of {elu_the} have started saying that this time it will last. You remember the last lot who said that, and where they are. There are garlands on the wall again. A very small child has brought one all the way up the hill, for the big dog, and is not at all afraid.

choices.text: Let the child put it on

effects.log: It does. It is the same dog, or as near as makes no difference. It has done this before, and it sits very still.

choices.text: Tell the young gods nothing

effects.log: Let them have it. It is what it is for. You go back in and look at the stores.

events.text: A Hush is on the realm. The Pantheons have gone quiet, nobody has been seen at the great Assembly in some time, and the prayers come in thinner each year, in smaller voices. {elu_m} comes to tell you {em_he} has heard a thing that frightened {em_him}: on the east of the plain, in a valley, someone has stopped praying and has not noticed.

choices.text: Go down to the valley yourself

effects.log: You go. You do not say who you are. You mend a wall, and you leave. It is not a large miracle, and it seems to do.

choices.text: Let it be. They are allowed

effects.log: It is hard to say, and you say it. {elu_m} looks at you, and then at the valley, for a good while.

events.text: The Hush again. Old gods sit in their halls and do not answer letters. {elu_The} have been keeping up the border anyway, walking it every night, with nobody to report to and nothing coming. You went out to see. {elu_m} salutes you with great care. "You did not have to do this," you say. "No," {em_he} agrees, and goes on walking.

choices.text: Walk the next stretch beside {em_him}

effects.log: Nothing comes. It is a very fine night for it. You have walked this border before, and you had forgotten about the stars.

choices.text: Go back in, and let {em_him} have it

effects.log: It is {em_his} border now, in every way that matters. You leave the gate on the latch.

events.text: There is an Age of Storms on the realm. The thrones have begun to quarrel in earnest, and there is weather in places that have not had any since the making. {elu_m} has had the old spears brought out, and they are all a good deal shorter than you remember. {elu_The} look at the sky in a way you have not seen for long and long.

choices.text: Lead them yourself

effects.log: It is a poor idea, at your rank, and the whole sky sees it. You find you have missed it badly.

choices.text: Stand them at the plain's edge, and keep the rain falling

effects.log: Your farmers bring in the harvest with lightning on all sides. They will not ever know how much it took.

events.text: The storms have come back. The farmers on your plain have a saying about this, which you taught to someone, some time ago. {elu_m} is new, and has been told by every one of the older ones that this is nothing compared with last time. It was not nothing last time. You remember who told you that it was nothing compared with the time before.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} it is worse this time

effects.log: It is what no one has told {em_him}. {em_He} goes rather quiet, and sees to the straps.

choices.text: Tell {em_him} it is nothing

effects.log: You have the voice for it. {em_He} grins and goes off to tell the younger ones.

events.text: A Harvest Age: every shrine in the realm is full, and the offerings are coming in faster than anyone can count them. It is a very dangerous time. Every god is suddenly rich, and they are looking at each other. {elu_m} reports that three separate pantheons have asked after the health of your stores, in the kindest way.

choices.text: Give a great deal of it away

effects.log: There is much surprise. It is hard to raid somebody who has already sent you a large gift, and you have a great many friends for a while.

choices.text: Set {elu_the} on the granaries

effects.log: Nobody tries anything. They stand there for four hundred years, among the barley, getting very fat and rather dangerous.

events.text: The barns are full again. A young priest has come to you with a new accounting of how much your plain owes you, and it is a very large number, and you are asked what is to be done with it. It is the same number as the last time, near enough, and you have not been able to remember what you did. {elu_m} remembers.

choices.text: Ask {elu_m} what you did

effects.log: "You had it all given back, and then complained about it for six hundred years," {em_he} says. You do that again.

choices.text: Do something new

effects.log: It goes badly, as new things tend to. You have rather enjoyed yourself, and so has the priest.

events.text: The barracks of {elu_the} have been empty for a while now. Someone still sweeps them. The banner hangs in the hall over nobody, and the steward has begun, very carefully, to ask whether the rice set aside for them might go somewhere else. The name is still on the rolls. It is the only name there.

choices.text: Raise new ones under the old banner (600 taels)

effects.log: You walk the yard and choose again. The banner comes down, is beaten free of dust, and goes back up over living people.

choices.text: Send for {elu_m}

effects.log: {elu_m} comes at once, as if {em_he} had been waiting by the gate for the message. Perhaps {em_he} had.

choices.text: Stand the name down, honestly

effects.log: You have it entered: {elu_The}, stood down, nobody left to carry them. The banner goes up in the hall with the others. The record stays on the rolls, and it is not a bad one.

choices.text: Keep the barracks swept, for now

effects.log: The steward bows and goes on sweeping. One day you will have to answer him properly.

events.text: At the spring muster the clerk reads out the companies of your house one by one, and comes to {elu_the}. There is a pause, because nobody is left to answer. Somebody at the back laughs and stops. The clerk looks at you over the list with the brush in the air, waiting to be told what to write.

choices.text: "Write: raising anew." (600 taels)

effects.log: The clerk writes it. By the autumn muster there is somebody to answer to the name, a little too loudly, and nobody laughs.

choices.text: "Write {elu_m}'s name back in."

effects.log: The clerk writes it. When {elu_m} hears, {em_he} turns up with {em_his} old token, which {em_he} never did hand in.

choices.text: "Write: stood down."

effects.log: The clerk writes it, and draws the line under it neatly. {elu_The} are done. Their deeds stay on the page above the line, where anyone can read them.

choices.text: "Write nothing yet."

effects.log: The clerk lowers the brush and moves on. Next year the pause will be a little longer.

events.text: The Rolls of the Jade Court carry {elu_the} as a company in good standing, with nobody in it. A clerk has noticed, in the way of clerks up here, about a decade after it happened. The letter is very polite. It asks whether the heading is to be kept open, filled, or closed, and it encloses three forms.

choices.text: Fill it: call up new immortals (5 spirit stones)

effects.log: The form goes back filled. Within a few years there are people on the isle under the old banner, arguing over who sleeps by the window.

choices.text: Send a cloud-barge for {elu_m}

effects.log: {elu_m} comes on the next barge with {em_his} old token in {em_his} sleeve. "I kept it," {em_he} says. "Up here you learn to."

choices.text: Close the heading

effects.log: The heading is closed with a red line, which up here is a kind of honour. {elu_The} stay on the Rolls under it, every deed of theirs, for as long as there are Rolls.

choices.text: Send the forms back unsigned

effects.log: The clerk will write again. It may be a century. Up here that is hardly a delay.

events.text: There is a pavilion on your isle with the banner of {elu_the} over its door, and nobody has gone in or out of it for some years. The mist has got into it. Visitors from the other isles have begun to ask, with great tact, whether it is a shrine. It is a fair question, and you owe it an answer.

choices.text: Fill the pavilion again (5 spirit stones)

effects.log: Word goes round the Isles that the banner is taking names. The mist is chased out of the pavilion by a great deal of shouting.

choices.text: Ask {elu_m} to come home

effects.log: {elu_m} lands on the terrace one morning as if {em_he} had only stepped out, and goes straight in to open the shutters.

choices.text: Make it a shrine, then

effects.log: You let it be one. {elu_The} are done, and the pavilion keeps their banner and their record. Visitors bow at the door. Some of them knew the names.

choices.text: Let the mist keep it a while

effects.log: The mist keeps it. Nobody up here is in a hurry, and the pavilion is very patient.

events.text: Prayers keep coming in for {elu_the}, small ones, from your plain: a lost goat, a bad well, a bridge. Nobody is left to answer them. They pile up at the foot of your throne in a soft grey drift, and the Surveyors have begun to step around it. Something must be done about the drift, at least.

choices.text: Call up new ones from the prayers (5 faith)

effects.log: You read through the drift and call up those who asked for the bravest things. They stand on your plain, blinking. The drift goes down by a good deal.

choices.text: Call {elu_m} back to your plain

effects.log: {elu_m} comes up from wherever {em_he} had gone, and takes {em_his} old place on the plain as if it had been kept warm. The goat is found by evening.

choices.text: Close their page in the Book of Fates

effects.log: You write the last line yourself: {elu_The}, done, with every prayer they ever answered listed under the name. The drift goes quiet. Your plain will tell stories of them for a long while.

choices.text: Let the prayers wait

effects.log: They wait. Prayers are good at that. The drift grows a little higher every spring.

events.text: A god of a minor river climbs to your throne on behalf of the other small gods. It has been asked to find out whether {elu_the} still exist, since nobody has seen one of them for years, and, if they do not, whether it might apply. It is trembling a little, and shining.

choices.text: Take it, and others like it (5 faith)

effects.log: The river god is the first on the new rolls. A bridge god and the god of one particular well follow. They stand very straight.

choices.text: Tell it {elu_m} is coming back

effects.log: You send for {elu_m}, who comes, and takes the river god on as a junior. It is the proudest day in the history of that river.

choices.text: Tell it the company is done

effects.log: It bows and goes. {elu_The} are in the Book of Fates, under your hand, and the river god tells their story to its fish.

choices.text: Tell it you will think about it

effects.log: It goes back down to its river and waits there, shining a little, in case.

events.text: The woodpile where {elu_the} used to drill has grown over with weeds. Children play there now, at being {elu_the}, with sticks. One of them asked you yesterday where the real ones went. You did not have a good answer, and the child went back to the game.

choices.text: Call up new ones (600 taels)

effects.log: You go round the valley and ask again. It is harder the second time. The weeds are gone by the end of the week, and the children take their game elsewhere, sulking.

choices.text: Send word to {elu_m}

effects.log: {elu_m} turns up at the gate the next morning with a bundle and a hoe. "About time," {em_he} says.

choices.text: Give the name to the children

effects.log: You tell the valley that {elu_the} are done, and that the name is free for anyone who plays at it. The pillar keeps what they really did. The children have the rest.

choices.text: Let the weeds grow a while

effects.log: The children go on playing. They have got quite good.

events.text: The steward has brought you the year's accounts. There is a line in them, as there has been for some years, for the wages of {elu_the}, and next to it a zero in a very neat hand. The steward would like to know, without wishing to be a nuisance, how long the zero is meant to go on.

choices.text: "Until I find new ones. Now." (600 taels)

effects.log: The zero is crossed out. A new figure goes in beside it, rather a large one, and there are names under it by harvest.

choices.text: "Until {elu_m} comes back."

effects.log: You send for {elu_m}, who comes, and asks for the old wage and not a copper more. The steward writes it in, much relieved.

choices.text: "Strike the line."

effects.log: The steward strikes it, carefully, so it can still be read. {elu_The} are done. The pillar of your world keeps their name and what they did.

choices.text: "Leave the zero."

effects.log: The steward leaves it, and sighs, and will be back next year with the same page.
